definition_en: a measured extent of surface, or a part of a place, field, or situation
core_image: 一块被边界圈定的平面：有范围、可测量
scene: 建筑师在图纸上圈出一块空地，标出长宽。 The architect circled a plot on the drawing, marked its length and width, and calculated the area of the land.
sceneCN: 这里 area 是「面积」（第 2 个义项：可测量的表面范围）；句意：建筑师在图纸上圈出一块地，标出长宽，算出这块地的面积。

senses.title: Open ground: a vacant piece of land
senses.titleCN: 空地：一块空着的场地
senses.definition: a piece of ground that is open or not built on
senses.definitionCN: 一块空着、未建房子的地面
senses.example: The children played in the empty area behind the school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在学校后面的空地上玩。
senses.why: Latin area first meant 'level ground, open space', especially a threshing floor or building site. The word starts as a flat patch of ground with no building on it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 area 最初指“平坦的空地、开阔空间”，尤指打谷场或建筑用地。这个词的起点，就是一块没有建筑的平地。

senses.title: Measured surface: length times width
senses.titleCN: 面积：长与宽量出来的表面
senses.definition: the amount of surface enclosed within a boundary, measured in square units
senses.definitionCN: 边界内所围表面的量，用平方单位计量
senses.example: The area of the room is twelve square metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间的面积是十二平方米。
senses.why: Once the patch is bounded, it can be measured. Length multiplied by width turns the physical ground into a number, and that number is also called area.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这块地被边界围住，就可以测量。长乘宽把具体的地面变成一个数字，这个数字也叫 area。

senses.title: A region or district
senses.titleCN: 地区：划出的一片地方
senses.definition: a part of a country, city, or the world, often defined by its character or use
senses.definitionCN: 国家、城市或世界的一部分，常按其性质或用途划分
senses.example: This is a quiet residential area.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一个安静的住宅区。
senses.why: A bounded patch can be large enough to contain streets and buildings. The same word moves from a single plot to a whole district with its own character.
senses.whyCN: 一块有边界的平面可以大到容纳街道和建筑。同一个词从单块地扩展到整个有自身特点的地区。

senses.title: A part of a place used for one purpose
senses.titleCN: 专用场地：建筑内划出的功能空间
senses.definition: a part of a building or place set aside for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物或场所中为某项活动划出的一部分
senses.example: The waiting area is next to the ticket office.
senses.exampleCN: 等候区在售票处旁边。
senses.why: Inside a building, boundaries are drawn by function rather than by ownership. A corner marked off for waiting becomes a waiting area.
senses.whyCN: 在建筑内部，边界由功能而不是所有权划出。划出来供人等候的一角，就成了等候区。

senses.title: A field of study or activity
senses.titleCN: 领域：知识或活动的一片范围
senses.definition: a subject or branch of knowledge, or a kind of activity
senses.definitionCN: 学科分支，或某一类活动
senses.example: She works in the area of molecular biology.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事分子生物学领域的工作。
senses.why: Knowledge is imagined as land: each subject occupies a patch with boundaries. Working 'in an area' means working inside that patch.
senses.whyCN: 知识被想象成土地：每个学科占据一块有边界的地。work in an area 就是在这一片地里工作。

senses.title: A sphere of responsibility or concern
senses.titleCN: 职责范围：该管的一片事
senses.definition: the range of matters for which a person or group is responsible
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或团体负责的事务范围
senses.example: Parking is not my area, so please ask the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 停车不归我管，请问经理。
senses.why: Responsibility is also mapped as territory. What you are responsible for is the patch you cover, and outside it is someone else's area.
senses.whyCN: 责任也被画成地盘。你负责的事就是你覆盖的那块地，之外就是别人的 area。

senses.title: A marked zone in a sport
senses.titleCN: 运动区：球场上划出的区域
senses.definition: a marked part of a sports field with a special rule
senses.definitionCN: 运动场上有特殊规则的一块划线区域
senses.example: The goalkeeper may use his hands inside the penalty area.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员可以在禁区内用手触球。
senses.why: Sports fields are divided by painted lines. Each bounded zone has its own rules, so the physical area becomes a rule-defined area.
senses.whyCN: 运动场用画线分隔。每块有边界的区域都有自己的规则，于是物理上的 area 变成了规则定义的区域。

senses.title: A region of the body
senses.titleCN: 身体部位：身体的一片区域
senses.definition: a particular part of the body, especially in medicine
senses.definitionCN: 身体某一部位，尤用于医学
senses.example: The doctor felt a pain in the lower abdominal area.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在下腹部区域摸到疼痛。
senses.why: Anatomy treats the body as a map and draws boundaries around organs and regions. A painful patch is described as an area.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把身体当作地图，在器官和区域周围画界。疼痛的一块就被描述为一个 area。

senses.title: A point or aspect of a matter
senses.titleCN: 事项的一个方面：问题中的一块
senses.definition: one part of a problem or subject that is being considered
senses.definitionCN: 正在考虑的问题或主题中的一个部分
senses.example: We agree on most areas, but cost is still an area of disagreement.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在多数方面一致，但成本仍是分歧点。
senses.why: A complex matter can be divided into parts, as if each part occupied its own patch. An area of disagreement is one bounded part of the whole dispute.
senses.whyCN: 复杂的事情可以被分成若干部分，仿佛每部分各占一块地。an area of disagreement 就是整场争议中有边界的一块。

intro.en: Area is a Latin word for open ground that English borrowed in the 16th century. Its deepest origin is uncertain; the 'dry ground' explanation is only a hypothesis.
intro.cn: area 是 16 世纪英语借入的拉丁词，原指开阔地面。它最深的来源并不确定，“干燥地面”的解释只是一个假设。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'a vacant piece of ground', used of building sites and open plots.
items.cn: 最早记录于 16 世纪 30 年代，意为“一块空地”，用于建筑用地和开阔地块。

items.en: Latin area meant 'level ground, open space', and was used for threshing floors, playgrounds and building sites.
items.cn: 拉丁语 area 意为“平坦地面、开阔空间”，用于打谷场、游戏场和建筑用地。

items.en: The origin of Latin area is uncertain. It is perhaps an irregular derivation from arere 'to become dry', on the idea of ground cleared by burning; this link is not proved.
items.cn: 拉丁语 area 的来源不确定。它也许与 arere“变干”有不规则派生关系，指烧荒清出的地面；这一联系并未得到证实，属来源不确定。

items.en: The measured sense 'surface contained within limits' appears in the 1560s; geometry later makes it a standard term for length times width.
items.cn: “边界内所围表面”的测量义出现于 16 世纪 60 年代；几何学后来把它固定为长乘宽的标准术语。

items.en: Modern English extends area to districts, fields of study and zones of responsibility. Area code is recorded from 1959, and areal is the adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语把 area 扩展到地区、研究领域和责任范围。area code（电话区号）记录于 1959 年，形容词是 areal。

note.en: The first group is about similar spelling and sound; the second is about words that also name a bounded part.
note.cn: 第一组看拼写和读音，第二组看同样表示“有边界的一部分”的词。

entries.definition: a long solo song in an opera. It differs by one letter and is unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 歌剧中的独唱咏叹调。只差一个字母，词义毫无关系。

entries.definition: a central stage or sports ground surrounded by seats. It shares the open-space idea but comes from Latin harena 'sand'.
entries.definitionCN: 四周有座位的中央舞台或运动场。它也含“开阔场地”之意，但来自拉丁语 harena“沙”。

entries.definition: the present plural of be; also a metric unit of land. It is pronounced differently and is a different word.
entries.definitionCN: be 的现在时复数形式；也指公制面积单位“公亩”。读音不同，是另一个词。

entries.definition: a large area of land, or a part with a shared feature. It is usually larger than an area.
entries.definitionCN: 大片地区，或具有共同特征的一部分。通常比 area 更大。

entries.definition: an area marked off for a special purpose or rule. It stresses the boundary and the rule more than area does.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途或规则划出的区域。它比 area 更强调边界和规则。

entries.definition: a branch of study or activity. In this sense it is close to area, but more abstract and more common in academic writing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或活动的分支。此义接近 area，但更抽象，也更常用于学术写作。

entries.definition: a part of a city or country with an official boundary. It is usually an administrative unit.
entries.definitionCN: 城市或国家中有官方边界的一部分，通常是行政单位。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin image of open ground, the geometry formula, and the area family in English.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语“空地”的意象、几何公式，以及英语中的 area 词族。

normal.en: Latin area meant a threshing floor, a flat open patch where grain was spread out. That flat patch is the core of the word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 area 指打谷场，即把谷子摊开的平坦空地。这块平地就是这个词的核心。

normal.en: Area in geometry is length × width: a bounded rectangle is measured and turned into a number.
normal.cn: 几何中的 area 是长 × 宽：一个有边界的矩形被测量，然后变成一个数字。

normal.en: An area of study is knowledge mapped as land: each subject occupies its own patch.
normal.cn: an area of study 是把知识画成土地：每个学科占自己的一块地。

normal.en: An area of responsibility is the territory you cover at work; outside it belongs to someone else.
normal.cn: an area of responsibility 是你在工作中覆盖的地盘；之外属于别人。

normal.en: Areal, areaway and area code keep the same bounded-surface idea in adjectives, buildings and telephone districts.
normal.cn: areal、areaway、area code 在形容词、建筑和电话分区中保留了同一个“有边界表面”的概念。

abstract.en: Abstractly, area is a surface plus a boundary: the boundary makes it countable, and counting turns it into measure.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，area 是“表面 + 边界”：边界让它可数，可数又让它变成度量。

abstract.en: The same boundary can be physical (a field), functional (a waiting area), social (a district) or mental (a field of study).
abstract.cn: 同一种边界可以是物理的（田地）、功能的（等候区）、社会的（地区）或心理的（研究领域）。

abstract.en: So area moves from ground to geometry, then to knowledge and responsibility, without changing its shape: a bounded patch.
abstract.cn: 所以 area 从地面走向几何，再走向知识与责任，而形状始终没变：一块有边界的平面。

examples.en: The fire spread over a large area of forest.
examples.cn: 大火蔓延到一大片森林区域。

examples.en: Please calculate the area of this rectangle.
examples.cn: 请计算这个矩形的面积。

examples.en: Language testing is her main area of research.
examples.cn: 语言测试是她的主要研究领域。

dict_mnemonic.text: “艾瑞尔”——艾瑞尔在图纸上圈地、量长宽算面积 → area 面积、区域

root: 拉丁语 area“空地、平坦地面”，词源不确定，可能与 arere“变干”有关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of area, all built on one shape: a surface enclosed by a boundary. The boundary may be physical, functional, administrative or mental, but the patch stays measurable.
sensesIntro.cn: area 的九个义项都建立在一个形状上：被边界围住的表面。边界可以是物理的、功能的、行政的或心理的，但这块平面始终可度量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat surface with a boundary drawn around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块画了边界的平面。

branches.en: OPEN GROUND: the original Latin sense, a vacant flat patch such as a threshing floor.
branches.cn: 空地：最古老的拉丁义，指打谷场那样一块空着的平地。

branches.en: MEASURE: once bounded, the surface can be measured as length × width.
branches.cn: 测量：一旦有了边界，表面就可以用长 × 宽来度量。

branches.en: REGION: the patch can be a district, a marked sports zone, or a mapped part of the body.
branches.cn: 区域：这块地可以是地区、球场上的划线区域，也可以是身体上被划分的部位。

branches.en: FUNCTION: inside a building, the boundary is drawn by use, producing a waiting or dining area.
branches.cn: 功能：在建筑内部，边界按用途划出，于是产生等候区或用餐区。

branches.en: FIELD: knowledge, responsibility and one part of an argument are all mapped as bounded territory.
branches.cn: 领域：知识、责任以及争论中的一个部分，都被画成有边界的地盘。

intro.en: Area is a Latin loanword, not built from living English affixes. English adds -al and -s, and forms compounds such as area code and areaway.
intro.cn: area 是拉丁借词，并不是由活的英语词缀构成的。英语给它加 -al、-s，并构成 area code、areaway 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin area has the diminutive areola 'small open space'. The metric unit are was coined from Latin area in 1795. A link with arere 'be dry' and arid is possible but not certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 area 有指小形式 areola“小块空地”。公制单位 are（公亩）于 1795 年由拉丁语 area 造出。它与 arere“变干”及 arid 的联系可能存在，但并不确定。

items.meaning: relating to an area
items.meaningCN: 面积的；区域的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Areal studies compare two regions.
items.exampleCN: 区域研究比较两个地区。

items.meaning: in terms of area
items.meaningCN: 按面积地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two districts are areally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两个区在面积上相似。

items.meaning: a smaller area within a larger one
items.meaningCN: 分区；子区域（sub- 表示“在下、次级”）
items.example: Each subarea has its own manager.
items.exampleCN: 每个分区都有自己的经理。

items.meaning: more than one subarea
items.meaningCN: 多个分区（-s 构成复数）
items.example: The province is divided into five subareas.
items.exampleCN: 这个省被分成五个分区。

items.meaning: affecting the whole area
items.meaningCN: 全区域的（-wide 表示“遍及”）
items.example: The area-wide power cut lasted two hours.
items.exampleCN: 全区停电持续了两个小时。

items.meaning: the number that identifies a telephone region
items.meaningCN: 电话区号（area + code 复合名词）
items.example: What is the area code for this city?
items.exampleCN: 这个城市的区号是多少？

items.meaning: academic study of one region's language, history and society
items.meaningCN: 区域研究（area + studies 复合名词）
items.example: She specializes in East Asian area studies.
items.exampleCN: 她专攻东亚区域研究。

items.meaning: a graph that fills the space under a line
items.meaningCN: 面积图（area + chart 复合名词）
items.example: The area chart shows sales over time.
items.exampleCN: 面积图显示销售额随时间的变化。

items.meaning: a passage or open space beside a building
items.meaningCN: 建筑物旁的空地或通道（area + way 复合名词）
items.example: They stored the bins in the areaway.
items.exampleCN: 他们把垃圾桶放在楼旁的空地上。

items.meaning: covering a large geographical area
items.meaningCN: 广域的；覆盖大范围的（wide + area 复合形容词）
items.example: The company runs a wide-area network.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司运营一个广域网络。

latinEntries.meaning: a metric unit of land equal to 100 square metres
latinEntries.meaningCN: 公亩（等于 100 平方米，由拉丁语 area 经法语造出）

latinEntries.meaning: a small open space; in anatomy, a small ring of colour around a nipple
latinEntries.meaningCN: 小空隙；（解剖）乳晕（area 的指小形式）

latinEntries.meaning: very dry; without moisture
latinEntries.meaningCN: 干旱的；无水的（与 arere“变干”同源，但与 area 的关系存疑）

definition_en: to come into being, occur, or move upward from a position
core_image: 从下方升起、从无到有地冒出来
scene: 会议进行到一半，有人举手提到预算表上的问题。 Halfway through the meeting a new budget problem began to arise in the discussion.
sceneCN: 这里 arise 是「出现、产生」（第 3 个义项：某事发生）；句意：会议进行到一半，一个新的预算问题在讨论中开始出现。

pos.zh: 出现；发生；产生；（文）起身、起义

derivatives.zh: 出现；产生（多用于法律用语）

senses.title: Get up from lying or sitting
senses.titleCN: 起身：从躺或坐的姿势站起来
senses.definition: to stand up from a sitting or lying position; literary in modern English
senses.definitionCN: 从坐或躺的姿势站起；现代英语中多为书面语
senses.example: He arose from his chair and opened the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他从椅子上起身，打开了窗户。
senses.why: Old English arisan meant 'to get up'. The a- prefix adds the idea of upward movement, so the body moves from a lower position to standing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 arisan 意为“起身”。前缀 a- 加上“向上”的意思，于是身体从较低的位置移动到站立。

senses.title: Come into being
senses.titleCN: 产生：从无到有地出现
senses.definition: to begin to exist, especially as a new thing or situation
senses.definitionCN: 开始存在，尤指新事物或新情况
senses.example: New industries arose along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 沿河兴起了新的产业。
senses.why: When something arises, it was not there before and now is. The upward image becomes a metaphor for emergence from nothing.
senses.whyCN: 某物 arise 时，它此前不在，现在在了。向上的意象变成“从无到有冒出来”的隐喻。

senses.title: Occur or happen
senses.titleCN: 发生：某事突然出现
senses.definition: to happen or occur, especially when not planned
senses.definitionCN: 发生，尤指并非计划中的事
senses.example: I will call you if the need arises.
senses.exampleCN: 如果有需要，我会打电话给你。
senses.why: A need or chance 'comes up' in time. Arise treats the event as something rising into the present, not as something scheduled.
senses.whyCN: 需要或机会在时间中“冒上来”。arise 把事件看作升入当下的事，而不是被安排的事。

senses.title: Result from a cause
senses.titleCN: 由……引起：作为结果产生
senses.definition: to be caused by or result from something
senses.definitionCN: 由某事物引起或作为其结果产生
senses.example: Most of these errors arise from careless reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这些错误大多源于粗心阅读。
senses.why: An effect can be pictured as rising out of its cause, the way a plant rises from soil. Arise from marks the source.
senses.whyCN: 结果可以被想象为从原因中长出来，像植物从土里升起。arise from 标出这个来源。

senses.title: Present itself to the mind
senses.titleCN: 浮现：在头脑或讨论中出现
senses.definition: to come to mind or into a discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中或讨论中出现
senses.example: A doubt arose in her mind.
senses.exampleCN: 她心里生出一个疑问。
senses.why: Thoughts and questions also 'come up'. What arises in the mind appears from below the surface of attention.
senses.whyCN: 想法和问题也会“冒上来”。在头脑中 arise 的东西，从注意力的表面之下浮现。

senses.title: Rise in opposition
senses.titleCN: 起义：起身反抗
senses.definition: to rebel or rise up against authority; literary
senses.definitionCN: 起来反抗权威；书面语
senses.example: The peasants arose against the heavy taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 农民起义反抗沉重的赋税。
senses.why: The physical act of standing up becomes political: a group rises from a subordinate position to challenge those above.
senses.whyCN: 起身这个物理动作变成政治动作：一群人从低位站起来，挑战在上者。

senses.title: Move upward
senses.titleCN: 升起：向上移动
senses.definition: to move upward, especially as mist, smoke, or the sun; literary
senses.definitionCN: 向上移动，尤指雾、烟或太阳；书面语
senses.example: Mist arose from the valley at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时雾从山谷升起。
senses.why: This is the literal upward branch. The same verb describes anything that leaves a lower level and moves into the air.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的向上分支。同一个动词描述任何离开低处、进入空中的东西。

senses.title: Rise to prominence
senses.titleCN: 崛起：上升到显要位置
senses.definition: to emerge as an important person or power
senses.definitionCN: 作为重要人物或力量出现
senses.example: A new leader arose during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机中崛起了一位新领袖。
senses.why: Social rank is imagined as height. A person who becomes important rises from the crowd, so arise can mean 'come to prominence'.
senses.whyCN: 社会地位被想象成高度。变得重要的人从人群里升起来，因此 arise 可以表示“崛起”。

senses.title: Arise under or out of a legal matter
senses.titleCN: 法律上由……产生
senses.definition: to be caused by or fall within a legal agreement, rule, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 由法律协议、规则或情形引起，或属于其范围
senses.example: Any dispute arising under this contract goes to arbitration.
senses.exampleCN: 由本合同产生的任何争议都提交仲裁。
senses.why: Legal English uses arise for rights and duties that come into existence from a document. The effect rises out of the clause that creates it.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语用 arise 表示由文件产生的权利和义务。结果从创设它的条款中产生。

intro.en: Arise is an Old English verb built from a- 'up' and rise. It has been largely replaced by rise except in abstract and legal contexts.
intro.cn: arise 是古英语动词，由 a-“向上”和 rise 构成。除抽象和法律语境外，它大多已被 rise 取代。

items.en: arisan meant 'to get up from sitting, kneeling, or lying; come into being; spring up; ascend'. It was a strong verb with past tense aras and past participle arisen.
items.cn: arisan 意为“从坐、跪或躺的姿势起身；产生；涌起；上升”。它是强动词，过去式 aras，过去分词 arisen。

items.en: The verb goes back to *us-risanan 'to go up', with cognates in Old Saxon arisan and Gothic urreisan.
items.cn: 该动词可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *us-risanan“向上走”，在古撒克逊语 arisan 和哥特语 urreisan 中有同源词。

items.en: OED states that no related terms have been traced outside Germanic, and one proposal is a lost European substrate word. The deeper origin is therefore source uncertain.
items.cn: 《牛津英语词典》指出，日耳曼语之外没有找到相关词；有一种推测认为它来自已消失的欧洲底层语言。因此更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English arisen narrowed toward 'come about, happen, originate', while rise took over most physical uses.
items.cn: 中古英语 arisen 向“发生、产生、起源”收窄，而多数物理用法被 rise 接管。

items.en: Modern English keeps arise mainly for circumstances, problems and legal consequences, as in the question arises and disputes arising under the contract.
items.cn: 现代英语的 arise 主要用于情况、问题和法律后果，如 the question arises、disputes arising under the contract。

note.en: The first group is about form and sound; the second is about other verbs of happening and beginning.
note.cn: 第一组看词形和读音，第二组看其他表示“发生、开始”的动词。

entries.definition: to lift or increase something; it is transitive and needs an object. Arise is intransitive and means 'come up'.
entries.definitionCN: 举起；提高；是及物动词，需要宾语。arise 是不及物动词，意为“出现”。

entries.definition: the past tense of arise. Do not confuse it with arouse 'to awaken a feeling'.
entries.definitionCN: arise 的过去式。不要与 arouse“唤起（感情）”混淆。

entries.definition: the past participle of arise, used after have or be.
entries.definitionCN: arise 的过去分词，用于 have 或 be 之后。

entries.definition: to awaken a feeling or response; it is transitive and has a different vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 唤起（感情或反应）；是及物动词，元音也不同。

entries.definition: to come out from hidden or early stage into view. It stresses visibility more than arise.
entries.definitionCN: 从隐蔽或早期阶段进入视野。它比 arise 更强调“显现”。

entries.definition: to happen, especially of events. It is more neutral and does not carry the upward image.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，尤指事件。它更中性，不带“向上”的意象。

entries.definition: to begin in a particular place or from a particular cause. It stresses the source.
entries.definitionCN: 始于某地或某因。它更强调源头。

entries.definition: to happen as an effect of something. It is the plainest word for cause and effect.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某事物的结果而发生。它是最直白的因果词。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: a- 'up' + rise, plus the strong pattern arise – arose – arisen and fixed phrases with from/in.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：a-“向上”+ rise，加上强变化 arise – arose – arisen，以及 from/in 的固定搭配。

normal.en: a- 'up' + rise = 'rise up'. The oldest sense is simply getting up from a low position.
normal.cn: a-“向上”+ rise =“升起来”。最古老的意思就是从低处起身。

normal.en: The strong forms are arise – arose – arisen, not *arised. The vowel changes just as in rise – rose – risen.
normal.cn: 强变化是 arise – arose – arisen，不是 *arised。元音变化与 rise – rose – risen 一样。

normal.en: Arise from marks a cause: errors arise from carelessness. The cause is the ground the effect rises out of.
normal.cn: arise from 标出原因：errors arise from carelessness。原因就是结果从中升起的土地。

normal.en: The question arises is a fixed academic phrase for a point that comes up in discussion.
normal.cn: the question arises 是学术写作的固定说法，表示讨论中出现一个问题。

normal.en: Legal English says disputes arising under a contract: the dispute rises out of the clause.
normal.cn: 法律英语说 disputes arising under a contract：争议从条款中产生。

abstract.en: Abstractly, arise is upward emergence: something moves from below the surface of a situation into view.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，arise 是“向上浮现”：某物从情况的表面之下进入视野。

abstract.en: The same movement covers a body standing up, a mist rising, a problem appearing, and a leader rising to power.
abstract.cn: 同一种运动涵盖身体站起、雾气上升、问题出现，以及领袖崛起掌权。

abstract.en: So the upward image is not decoration: it explains why arise is intransitive. Things arise by themselves; you raise something else.
abstract.cn: 所以“向上”的意象不是装饰：它解释了为什么 arise 是不及物动词。事物自己 arise；你 raise 别的东西。

examples.en: A serious problem arose during the test.
examples.cn: 测试过程中出现了一个严重问题。

examples.en: The misunderstanding arose from a mistranslation.
examples.cn: 这个误解源于一处误译。

examples.en: Please contact us if any difficulty arises.
examples.cn: 如果出现任何困难，请联系我们。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿赖兹”——阿赖兹从椅子上站起来，新问题也跟着冒出来 → arise 起身、出现

root: 古英语 arisan = a-“向上”+ risan“升起”，核心是“从下往上冒出来”；更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of arise, all versions of upward emergence: a body gets up, a thing begins, an event happens, an effect comes from a cause, a thought surfaces, a group rebels, mist rises, a leader emerges, and a legal right arises from a clause.
sensesIntro.cn: arise 的九个义项都是“向上浮现”的变体：身体起身、事物产生、事件发生、结果由原因而来、想法浮现、群体起义、雾气上升、领袖崛起，以及法律权利由条款产生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something moves upward from below and comes into view.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物从下方升起并进入视野。

branches.en: PHYSICAL RISE: a body stands up, or mist and smoke move upward.
branches.cn: 物理上升：身体站起来，或雾与烟向上移动。

branches.en: EMERGENCE: a new thing begins to exist, or a person rises to prominence.
branches.cn: 涌现：新事物开始存在，或一个人崛起而显要。

branches.en: COMING UP: an event happens, or a thought surfaces in the mind.
branches.cn: 冒出来：一个事件发生，或一个想法在头脑中浮现。

branches.en: CAUSE: an effect rises out of its source, including a legal consequence out of a clause.
branches.cn: 因果：结果从来源中升起，也包括由条款产生的法律后果。

branches.en: REBELLION: standing up becomes political resistance.
branches.cn: 反抗：起身这个动作变成政治上的抵抗。

intro.en: Arise shares the rise family. English adds -ing and the past participle arisen, and prefixes re- and up- to the base.
intro.cn: arise 与 rise 词族共用词根。英语加 -ing 和过去分词 arisen，并用 re-、up- 前缀构成新词。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin cognate for arise. OED finds no related terms outside Germanic, so the Latin list is left empty rather than filled with guesswork.
latinIntro.cn: arise 没有可靠的拉丁同族词。《牛津英语词典》在日耳曼语之外没有找到相关词，因此拉丁词条留空，而不是用猜测填充。

items.meaning: the act of coming into being, especially in legal texts
items.meaningCN: 出现；产生（-ing 构成动名词，多见于法律文本）
items.example: All claims arising are listed in the contract.
items.exampleCN: 合同列出了由此产生的所有索赔。

items.meaning: having come into being; having risen
items.meaningCN: 已出现的；已升起的（过去分词）
items.example: The problems that have arisen are serious.
items.exampleCN: 已经出现的问题很严重。

items.meaning: to come up again
items.meaningCN: 再次出现（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: The same question may re-arise later.
items.exampleCN: 同样的问题以后可能再次出现。

items.meaning: to rise up; to rebel; literary
items.meaningCN: 升起；起义（up- 表示“向上”；书面语）
items.example: The people uprose against the ruler.
items.exampleCN: 人民起义反抗统治者。

items.meaning: a rebellion or revolt
items.meaningCN: 起义；暴动（-ing 构成名词）
items.example: The uprising was quickly suppressed.
items.exampleCN: 起义很快被镇压。

items.meaning: the time when the sun comes up
items.meaningCN: 日出（sun + rise 复合词）
items.example: We left before sunrise.
items.exampleCN: 我们在日出前离开。

items.meaning: to move upward or increase
items.meaningCN: 升起；上升；增加（基础动词）
items.example: Prices rose sharply last year.
items.exampleCN: 去年物价急剧上涨。

items.meaning: going up; increasing
items.meaningCN: 上升的；增加的（-ing 构成形容词或名词）
items.example: Rising costs worry the factory.
items.exampleCN: 不断上升的成本让工厂担忧。

items.meaning: a person who gets up, or a vertical part such as a stair riser
items.meaningCN: 起身的人；楼梯踢面（-er 表示做动作的人或物）
items.example: The early riser caught the first train.
items.exampleCN: 早起的人赶上了第一班火车。

items.meaning: a tall building with many floors
items.meaningCN: 高层的；高层建筑（high + rise 复合词）
items.example: They live in a high-rise apartment.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一栋高层公寓里。

definition_en: a particular part or view of something, or the way it looks or faces
core_image: 同一物体转到不同角度，露出不同的一面
scene: 中介站在房子背后，手里拿着指南针。 The agent checked the compass and confirmed that the aspect of the house was toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 aspect 是「朝向」（第 5 个义项：建筑或坡面所朝的方向）；句意：中介查看指南针，确认这栋房子的朝向是大海。

senses.title: A part or feature of a whole
senses.titleCN: 方面：整体中的一个部分
senses.definition: one part of a situation, problem, or subject
senses.definitionCN: 情况、问题或主题的一个部分
senses.example: We must consider every aspect of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须考虑计划的每个方面。
senses.why: Latin aspectus is 'a look'. When you look at a whole from one angle, one face of it comes into view; that face is an aspect.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aspectus 是“一看”。当你从一个角度看整体，它的一面进入视野；这一面就是一个 aspect。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.titleCN: 角度：看事情的方式
senses.definition: a particular way of viewing a subject
senses.definitionCN: 观察某一主题的特定方式
senses.example: From a legal aspect, the contract is invalid.
senses.exampleCN: 从法律角度看，这份合同无效。
senses.why: The viewer's position determines which face is seen. Aspect can therefore mean the angle itself, not only the feature seen.
senses.whyCN: 观看者的位置决定看到哪一面。因此 aspect 也可以指角度本身，而不只是被看到的那一面。

senses.title: Outward appearance of a thing
senses.titleCN: 外观：事物呈现的样子
senses.definition: the appearance of something as it presents itself
senses.definitionCN: 某物呈现出来的样子
senses.example: The valley took on a green aspect in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天里山谷呈现出绿色。
senses.why: Aspect first meant the look of a thing. Appearance is what the surface shows to a viewer, before any deeper analysis.
senses.whyCN: aspect 最初指事物的外观。外观是表层向观看者展示的东西，在深入分析之前就能看到。

senses.title: Facial expression
senses.titleCN: 神情：脸上的样子
senses.definition: the expression on a person's face
senses.definitionCN: 一个人脸上的表情
senses.example: His aspect was calm, but his hands were shaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他神情平静，双手却在发抖。
senses.why: The face is the surface we read for emotion. The old sense 'countenance' treats the face as the visible aspect of the inner state.
senses.whyCN: 脸是我们读取情绪的表面。旧义“面容”把脸看作内在状态可见的一面。

senses.title: Direction faced by a building or slope
senses.titleCN: 朝向：建筑或坡面所对的方向
senses.definition: the direction in which a building, room, or slope faces
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、房间或坡面所朝的方向
senses.example: A southern aspect gives the room more winter sun.
senses.exampleCN: 朝南的朝向让房间在冬天得到更多阳光。
senses.why: A surface has a front, and that front points somewhere. Aspect moves from 'look' to the direction from which light and weather arrive.
senses.whyCN: 表面有正面，而正面指向某处。aspect 从“外观”转为光线和天气到来的方向。

senses.title: Astrological position
senses.titleCN: 星象：行星的相对位置
senses.definition: the relative position of planets as seen from earth; historical astrology
senses.definitionCN: 从地球看行星的相对位置；历史上的占星用法
senses.example: The two planets were in a favourable aspect.
senses.exampleCN: 两颗行星处于有利的相位。
senses.why: Astrology reads the sky as a face: how planets look at one another from earth is their aspect. The word entered English first in this technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 占星术把天空当作一张脸：行星从地球看如何彼此相对，就是它们的 aspect。这个词最早正是以这一术语义进入英语。

senses.title: Grammatical aspect
senses.titleCN: 语法体：动词表示的动作阶段
senses.definition: the grammatical form that shows whether an action is ongoing, completed, or repeated
senses.definitionCN: 表示动作持续、完成或反复的语法形式
senses.example: English marks progressive aspect with be + -ing.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用 be + -ing 标记进行体。
senses.why: Grammar views an event from a particular point: is it a point, a process, or a completed whole? That view is called aspect.
senses.whyCN: 语法从特定角度看待事件：它是一个点、一个过程，还是一个完成的整体？这种视角就叫 aspect。

senses.title: A view or scene
senses.titleCN: 景象：眼前展开的景色
senses.definition: a view or scene presented to the eye; literary
senses.definitionCN: 呈现在眼前的景色；书面语
senses.example: The garden presented a cheerful aspect.
senses.exampleCN: 花园呈现出宜人的景象。
senses.why: The oldest visual sense survives in literary description. What the eye takes in from one position is the aspect of the scene.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的视觉义保留在文学描写中。眼睛从一个位置看到的整体，就是景色的 aspect。

intro.en: Aspect entered English as an astrological term and comes from the Latin verb 'to look at'. Its history is a chain of seeing: look, appearance, face, direction, and finally a grammatical view.
intro.cn: aspect 以占星术语进入英语，来自拉丁语“看”的动词。它的历史是一条“看”的链条：看、外观、面容、朝向，最后是语法上的视角。

items.en: First recorded as an astrological term for the relative position of planets as they appear from earth, and also for 'one of the ways of viewing something'.
items.cn: 最早记录为占星术语，指行星从地球看来的相对位置，也指“看待某事物的一种方式”。

items.en: From Latin aspectus 'a seeing, look, sight, view; countenance; appearance', from the past participle of aspicere 'to look at'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 aspectus“看见、目光、景象、面容、外观”，出自 aspicere“朝……看”的过去分词。

items.en: aspicere = ad- 'to, toward' + specere 'to look'. The prefix directs the gaze; the root supplies the seeing.
items.cn: aspicere = ad-“朝向”+ specere“看”。前缀把目光指向某处，词根提供“看”的动作。

items.en: specere goes back to PIE *spek- 'to observe', the root behind inspect, prospect, respect, perspective and spectacle.
items.cn: specere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *spek-“观察”，inspect、prospect、respect、perspective、spectacle 都出自这个词根。

items.en: The senses 'the look one wears' and 'the appearance of things' are recorded by the early 15th century.
items.cn: “一个人脸上的神情”和“事物的外观”这两个义项在 15 世纪初已有记录。

items.en: The sense 'a facing in a given direction' appears in the 1660s. Grammar adopts aspect for verb aspect in the 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: “朝向某个方向”的义项出现于 17 世纪 60 年代。语法学在 19、20 世纪用 aspect 指动词的“体”。

note.en: The first group shares the spec- 'look' root or looks similar; the second names other ways of talking about a part or a view.
note.cn: 第一组共享 spec-“看”的词根或词形相近；第二组是其他表示“部分或视角”的词。

entries.definition: to think something will happen. It also contains specere 'look', but the prefix ex- means 'out'.
entries.definitionCN: 预料某事会发生。它也含 specere“看”，但前缀 ex- 表示“向外”。

entries.definition: to look closely at something. in- 'into' + specere 'look' gives 'look into'.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细检查。in-“进入”+ specere“看”即“看进去”。

entries.definition: to admire or honour; also a particular point. re- 'back' + specere 'look' gives 'look back at'.
entries.definitionCN: 尊敬；方面。re-“回”+ specere“看”即“回看”。

entries.definition: the word itself; do not confuse its noun ending -pect with the verb suspect.
entries.definitionCN: 本词；注意名词词尾 -pect 不要与动词 suspect 混淆。

entries.definition: a distinctive part of something. It is more concrete and often a visible characteristic.
entries.definitionCN: 某物有辨识度的一部分。它更具体，常指可见特征。

entries.definition: one side of a subject, like a cut face of a gem. It is more formal and more clearly one of several sides.
entries.definitionCN: 主题的一面，像宝石切出的一个面。它更正式，也更明确地表示若干面之一。

entries.definition: one of two or more aspects of a situation, especially in the phrase one side of the story.
entries.definitionCN: 情况的两个或多个方面之一，尤用于 one side of the story。

entries.definition: a way of approaching a subject. It stresses the viewer's position rather than the feature seen.
entries.definitionCN: 切入主题的方式。它更强调观看者的位置，而不是被看到的特点。

entries.definition: the way something looks. It is broader than aspect and does not imply viewing from one side.
entries.definitionCN: 某物看起来的样子。它比 aspect 更宽，不暗示从某一面看。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- 'to' + specere 'look', the spec- family, and the grammar term for verb aspect.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad-“朝向”+ specere“看”、spec- 词族，以及动词“体”的语法术语。

normal.en: ad- 'toward' + specere 'look' = 'look toward'. An aspect is one face of something as seen from a particular direction.
normal.cn: ad-“朝向”+ specere“看”=“朝……看”。aspect 就是从某个方向看到的某一面。

normal.en: Inspect, respect, prospect, perspective and spectacle all contain the same spec- 'look' root.
normal.cn: inspect、respect、prospect、perspective、spectacle 都含同一个 spec-“看”的词根。

normal.en: A southern aspect is the side that looks south; the building's face points toward the sun.
normal.cn: a southern aspect 是朝南的一面；建筑的脸朝向太阳。

normal.en: Grammatical aspect is the view of an action: a point, an ongoing process, or a completed whole.
normal.cn: 语法上的 aspect 是对动作的视角：一个点、一个持续过程，还是一个完成的整体。

normal.en: An aspect ratio is the shape of a screen expressed as width to height, a measurable face of the display.
normal.cn: aspect ratio 是屏幕的形状，用宽与高表示，即显示器可度量的一面。

abstract.en: Abstractly, aspect is a viewing operation: choose a position, and one face of a whole appears while others turn away.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，aspect 是一种观看操作：选定位置，整体的一面出现，其他面转开。

abstract.en: The same operation produces a feature of a problem, an appearance, a facial expression, a direction, a planetary relation and a verb form.
abstract.cn: 同一种操作产生了问题的方面、外观、神情、朝向、行星相位和动词形式。

abstract.en: So aspect is not a list of unrelated meanings. It is one geometry: a whole with faces, and a viewer who can stand in different places.
abstract.cn: 所以 aspect 不是一堆无关的词义，而是一个几何关系：一个有多个面的整体，以及一个能站在不同位置的观看者。

examples.en: We discussed the financial aspect of the decision.
examples.cn: 我们讨论了这项决定的财务方面。

examples.en: The room has a southern aspect and gets plenty of light.
examples.cn: 这个房间朝南，采光充足。

examples.en: The progressive aspect describes an action in progress.
examples.cn: 进行体描述正在进行的动作。

dict_mnemonic.text: “爱斯派克”——爱斯派克绕到房子南面，看到它的朝向和海景 → aspect 朝向、外观、方面

root: 拉丁语 aspectus“看见、外观”，来自 aspicere = ad-“朝向”+ specere“看”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of aspect, all versions of one viewing operation: a whole has faces, and a viewer sees whichever face is turned toward him. The faces become a feature, a viewpoint, an appearance, a face, a direction, a planet's position, a verb form and a scene.
sensesIntro.cn: aspect 的八个义项都是一种观看操作的变体：整体有多个面，观看者看到转向自己的那一面。这些面成为方面、视角、外观、面容、朝向、行星位置、动词体和景象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole with many faces; the viewer sees the face turned toward him.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个有多个面的整体；观看者看到朝向自己的那一面。

branches.en: VISIBLE SURFACE: what the eye sees is an appearance, a facial expression, or a scene.
branches.cn: 可见表面：眼睛看到的是外观、神情或景象。

branches.en: DIRECTION: the face of a building or slope points toward light and weather.
branches.cn: 朝向：建筑或坡面的“脸”指向光线与天气来的方向。

branches.en: PART OF A WHOLE: one face of a matter, a feature among others.
branches.cn: 整体的一面：一件事的一个面，是若干特征之一。

branches.en: TECHNICAL VIEW: astrology reads planetary faces; grammar views an action as point, process or whole.
branches.cn: 技术视角：占星术读行星的相对面；语法把动作看成点、过程或整体。

branches.en: POINT OF VIEW: the angle from which a matter is considered.
branches.cn: 视角：观察一件事时所取的角度。

intro.en: Aspect is a Latin noun. English builds aspectual, aspectuality and compounds such as aspect ratio from it.
intro.cn: aspect 是拉丁名词。英语由它构成 aspectual、aspectuality，以及 aspect ratio 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on specere 'to look' (PIE *spek-): inspect, prospect, respect and perspective all describe a directed gaze.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 specere“看”（原始印欧语 *spek-）上：inspect、prospect、respect、perspective 都描述有方向的目光。

items.meaning: relating to aspect, especially grammatical aspect
items.meaningCN: （语法）体的；方面的（-ual 构成形容词）
items.example: Aspectual meaning is shown by the verb form.
items.exampleCN: 体意义由动词形式表示。

items.meaning: in terms of aspect
items.meaningCN: 从体或方面的角度（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two verbs are aspectually different.
items.exampleCN: 这两个动词在体上不同。

items.meaning: the quality of having aspect
items.meaningCN: 体性；方面性（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The paper studies aspectuality in Chinese.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文研究汉语的体性。

items.meaning: organized around aspects; used in programming
items.meaningCN: 面向方面的（aspect + oriented 复合形容词，编程术语）
items.example: Aspect-oriented programming separates cross-cutting concerns.
items.exampleCN: 面向方面编程把横切关注点分离出来。

items.meaning: the ratio of width to height of an image or screen
items.meaningCN: 纵横比；宽高比（aspect + ratio 复合名词）
items.example: The film has a wide aspect ratio.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片采用宽幅纵横比。

items.meaning: a grammatical word or affix that marks aspect
items.meaningCN: 体标记（aspectual + marker 复合名词）
items.example: The language uses a particle as an aspectual marker.
items.exampleCN: 这种语言用一个助词作体标记。

items.meaning: relating to an aspect; a rare adjective
items.meaningCN: 方面的；体相关的（-ive 构成形容词，较少见）
items.example: The aspective reading is only one interpretation.
items.exampleCN: 从方面角度的读法只是一种解释。

items.meaning: more than one aspect
items.meaningCN: 多个方面（-s 构成复数）
items.example: The report covers all aspects of the case.
items.exampleCN: 报告涵盖了案件的各个方面。

items.meaning: in terms of aspects; informal
items.meaningCN: 就各方面而言（-wise 构成副词，非正式）
items.example: Aspect-wise, the plan is sound.
items.exampleCN: 就各方面而言，这个计划是合理的。

latinEntries.meaning: to look closely into something
a view forward; a possibility in the future
to look back at someone with esteem; a particular point
a way of seeing through a scene; a viewpoint

definition_en: to bring people or parts together into one group or whole
core_image: 散落的零件或人被召集到同一处，拼成一个整体
scene: 工作台上散落着齿轮和轴承，旁边放着扳手。 The worker assembled the scattered parts into a complete engine.
sceneCN: 这里 assemble 是「组装」（第 3 个义项：把零件拼成整体）；句意：工人把散落的零件组装成了一台完整的发动机。

senses.title: People gather in one place
senses.titleCN: 聚集：人们来到同一处
senses.definition: to come together in one place as a group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个群体来到同一处
senses.example: The students assembled in the courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在院子里集合。
senses.why: Latin ad- 'to' + simul 'together' gives the idea of moving toward one common place. The first sense is simply people coming together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad-“向”+ simul“一起”给出“向同一处移动”的概念。第一个义项就是人们聚到一起。

senses.title: Bring people together
senses.titleCN: 召集：把人聚起来
senses.definition: to cause a group of people to come together
senses.definitionCN: 使一群人聚集起来
senses.example: The teacher assembled the class for a photo.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把全班召集起来拍照。
senses.why: The same gathering can be caused by someone. Assemble becomes transitive: a person or institution is the centre that pulls others in.
senses.whyCN: 同一种聚集也可以由某人促成。assemble 变成及物动词：一个人或机构成为把别人拉进来的中心。

senses.title: Put parts together into a whole
senses.titleCN: 组装：把零件拼成整体
senses.definition: to fit separate parts together to make a whole object
senses.definitionCN: 把分离的零件拼合成一个完整物体
senses.example: Workers assemble the engine on the line.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在流水线上组装发动机。
senses.why: Pieces are like people: they are scattered first, then brought to one place and fitted together. The manufacturing sense is recorded from 1852.
senses.whyCN: 零件也像人：先散在各处，再被带到一处拼合。制造业义记录于 1852 年。

senses.title: Install machinery from parts
senses.titleCN: 安装：把部件装成设备
senses.definition: to fit and install the parts of a machine or structure
senses.definitionCN: 把机器或结构的部件装配、安装起来
senses.example: The bed is easy to assemble at home.
senses.exampleCN: 这张床在家里很容易组装。
senses.why: Assembly is not only factory work. Furniture and equipment arrive in parts and are assembled where they will be used.
senses.whyCN: 装配不只在工厂。家具和设备以零件运来，在使用地点被组装起来。

senses.title: Compile documents or data
senses.titleCN: 汇编：把材料聚成一份
senses.definition: to collect and arrange information, evidence, or documents
senses.definitionCN: 收集并整理信息、证据或文件
senses.example: She assembled the evidence into a clear report.
senses.exampleCN: 她把证据汇编成一份清晰的报告。
senses.why: Information also arrives in pieces. Bringing those pieces into one file is the same movement from scattered to whole.
senses.whyCN: 信息也是以碎片到来。把这些碎片聚进一个文件，同样是“从散到整”的运动。

senses.title: Mobilize a team or force
senses.titleCN: 集结：召集队伍或力量
senses.definition: to gather people and resources for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的聚集人员和资源
senses.example: The company assembled a team of experts.
senses.exampleCN: 公司集结了一支专家团队。
senses.why: A team is assembled before action, just as parts are assembled before a machine runs. The word marks the moment of readiness.
senses.whyCN: 团队在行动前被集结，正如机器运转前零件被组装。这个词标出“准备就绪”的时刻。

senses.title: Build from a kit or puzzle
senses.titleCN: 拼装：按套件或拼图搭起来
senses.definition: to build something from a set of pieces, such as a kit or puzzle
senses.definitionCN: 用一套零件搭起某物，如套件或拼图
senses.example: The children assembled a model plane from a kit.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用套件拼装了一架模型飞机。
senses.why: A kit is a set of separated pieces with a plan. Assembling is the playful, small-scale version of industrial assembly.
senses.whyCN: 套件是一组分离的零件加一份图纸。拼装是工业装配的娱乐化、小尺度版本。

senses.title: Translate assembly code
senses.titleCN: 汇编：把汇编语言转成机器码
senses.definition: to convert assembly language into machine code; computing
senses.definitionCN: 把汇编语言转换成机器码；计算机术语
senses.example: The program assembles the source code into machine instructions.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把源代码汇编成机器指令。
senses.why: In computing, pieces of code are gathered and converted into one executable whole. The metaphor is still 'bring together and make usable'.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机中，代码片段被收集并转换成一个可执行的整体。隐喻仍是“聚起来并变得可用”。

senses.title: Summon a legislature or group
senses.titleCN: 召集：正式召集议会或团体
senses.definition: to summon a parliament, council, or official group; formal or historical
senses.definitionCN: 正式召集议会、委员会或官方团体；正式或历史用法
senses.example: The king assembled the council at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 国王在黎明时召集了议会。
senses.why: An authority can call a group into being for a session. This is the institutional version of people gathering in one place.
senses.whyCN: 权威可以召集一个团体开会。这是“人们聚到一处”的制度化版本。

intro.en: Assemble came to English from Old French and goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to make alike' and later 'to gather'. The modern manufacturing sense is surprisingly recent.
intro.cn: assemble 经古法语进入英语，可追溯到拉丁语“使相似”、后来“聚集”的动词。现代制造业义项其实出现得很晚。

items.en: First recorded in English as both transitive 'collect into one place' and intransitive 'meet or come together'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪初，既作及物动词“把……收集到一处”，也作不及物动词“相遇、聚在一起”。

items.en: From Old French assembler 'come together, join, unite; gather' (11c.), the source of Modern French assembler.
items.cn: 来自古法语 assembler“聚在一起、结合、联合；收集”（11 世纪），也是现代法语 assembler 的来源。

items.en: From Latin assimulare 'to make like, liken, compare; copy, imitate', later used for 'to gather together'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 assimulare“使相似、比拟、比较；复制、模仿”，后来用于“聚集在一起”。

items.en: assimulare = ad- 'to' + simulare 'to make like', from similis 'like, resembling'. The root is PIE *sem- 'one, together'.
items.cn: assimulare = ad-“向”+ simulare“使相似”，后者来自 similis“相似的”。词根是原始印欧语 *sem-“一、一起”。

items.en: The specific sense 'put parts together' in manufacturing is recorded from 1852, long after the word's general sense of gathering.
items.cn: 制造业中“把零件拼在一起”的具体义项记录于 1852 年，远晚于该词一般的“聚集”义。

items.en: Modern English uses assemble for people, parts, evidence and code. Assembly is the noun for both a meeting and a machine made of parts.
items.cn: 现代英语用 assemble 指人、零件、证据和代码。名词 assembly 既指集会，也指由零件组成的机器组件。

note.en: The first group is about the ass- spelling; the second is about other verbs of gathering and building.
note.cn: 第一组看 ass- 拼写，第二组看其他表示“聚集、搭建”的动词。

entries.definition: to suppose or take on. It shares the ass- opening but has no 'together' root.
entries.definitionCN: 假定；承担。它同样以 ass- 开头，但没有“一起”的词根。

entries.definition: to judge value. It comes from 'sit beside', not from 'gather together'.
entries.definitionCN: 评估价值。它来自“坐在旁边”，而不是“聚在一起”。

entries.definition: to help. It comes from 'stand beside', another different root.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助。它来自“站在旁边”，又是另一个词根。

entries.definition: the noun from assemble: a meeting, or the act of fitting parts.
entries.definitionCN: assemble 的派生名词：集会，或装配行为。

entries.definition: to bring people or things together. It is broader and more everyday than assemble.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或物聚在一起。它比 assemble 更宽、更日常。

entries.definition: to bring things together, especially over time. It stresses accumulation rather than fitting into a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西收集起来，尤指随着时间累积。它强调积累，而不是拼成整体。

entries.definition: to come together in a crowd. It is formal and usually intransitive.
entries.definitionCN: 成群聚集。它较正式，通常作不及物动词。

entries.definition: to build something from parts or materials. It stresses the finished structure more than the gathering act.
entries.definitionCN: 用零件或材料建造。它比“聚集动作”更强调建成的结构。

entries.definition: to collect information into a list or document. It is the usual word for assembling data.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息收集成清单或文件。它是“汇编数据”的常用词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- + simul 'together', the similis/*sem- family, and the assembly compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad- + simul“一起”、similis/*sem- 词族，以及 assembly 复合词。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + simul 'together' = 'bring to one place together'. That is the whole core of assemble.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ simul“一起”=“把……聚到一处”。这就是 assemble 的全部核心。

normal.en: Similar, simulate, assimilate and simultaneous share the *sem- 'one, together' root: likeness is being of one kind.
normal.cn: similar、simulate、assimilate、simultaneous 共享 *sem-“一、一起”词根：相似就是同类。

normal.en: Assembly is both a meeting and a machine part: people gathered, or parts gathered.
normal.cn: assembly 既是集会也是组件：人被聚起来，或零件被聚起来。

normal.en: Assembly line is a real compound: the line where parts are assembled one after another.
normal.cn: assembly line 是真实复合词：零件一个接一个被组装起来的流水线。

normal.en: Disassemble is the reverse: dis- 'apart' + assemble, to take the whole apart again.
normal.cn: disassemble 是反向动作：dis-“分开”+ assemble，把整体再拆开。

abstract.en: Abstractly, assemble is a centripetal operation: scattered elements are moved toward a centre and fitted into one whole.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，assemble 是一种向心操作：散落的元素被移向一个中心，拼成一个整体。

abstract.en: The elements can be people, machine parts, documents or lines of code; the operation is the same each time.
abstract.cn: 元素可以是人、机器零件、文件或代码行；每次的操作都一样。

abstract.en: So the word always marks a change of state: from scattered to gathered, from parts to whole, from potential to ready.
abstract.cn: 所以这个词总标出一种状态变化：从散到聚，从零件到整体，从潜在到就绪。

examples.en: The manager assembled a strong team for the project.
examples.cn: 经理为这个项目召集了一支强大的团队。

examples.en: It took two hours to assemble the bookshelf.
examples.cn: 组装这个书架花了两个小时。

examples.en: The crowd assembled outside the theatre.
examples.cn: 人群在剧院外聚集。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿森堡”——阿森堡把散落的零件都叫到一起，拼成一台机器 → assemble 集合、组装

root: 古法语 assembler“聚在一起”，源自拉丁语 ad-“向”+ simul“一起”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of assemble, all built on one movement: scattered elements are brought toward one centre and made into a whole. The elements may be people, parts, evidence, a team, a puzzle, code or a council.
sensesIntro.cn: assemble 的九个义项都建立在一个运动上：散落的元素被带向一个中心，组成整体。这些元素可以是人、零件、证据、团队、拼图、代码或议会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered pieces move toward one centre and fit into a whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的部件向一个中心聚拢，拼成整体。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a crowd comes together, or someone causes the crowd to come together.
branches.cn: 人：人群自己聚拢，或有人把人群召集起来。

branches.en: PARTS: machine parts, furniture parts and kit pieces are fitted into a working or complete object.
branches.cn: 零件：机器部件、家具部件和套件零件被装成能运转或完整的物体。

branches.en: INFORMATION: evidence and documents are collected and arranged into one report.
branches.cn: 信息：证据和文件被收集并整理成一份报告。

branches.en: MOBILIZATION: a team, force or council is summoned and made ready for a purpose.
branches.cn: 动员：团队、力量或议会为某个目的被召集并准备就绪。

branches.en: CODE: program pieces are gathered and converted into one executable whole.
branches.cn: 代码：程序片段被收集并转换成一个可执行的整体。

intro.en: English builds assembly, assembler, assembled, disassemble and reassemble from assemble. The -y noun and the dis-/re- prefixes are productive.
intro.cn: 英语由 assemble 构成 assembly、assembler、assembled、disassemble、reassemble。-y 名词和 dis-/re- 前缀都有能产性。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on similis 'like' and simul 'together' (PIE *sem- 'one'): similar, simulate, assimilate and simultaneous all belong here.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 similis“相似”和 simul“一起”（原始印欧语 *sem-“一”）上：similar、simulate、assimilate、simultaneous 都属于此。

items.meaning: a group gathered for a purpose, or the act of fitting parts
items.meaningCN: 集会；装配（-y 构成名词）
items.example: The assembly meets every Monday.
items.exampleCN: 集会每周一举行。

items.meaning: a person or machine that assembles; also a program that converts assembly code
items.meaningCN: 装配工；汇编程序（-er 表示做动作的人或物）
items.example: The assembler checks each part before fitting it.
items.exampleCN: 装配工在安装前检查每个零件。

items.meaning: brought together or fitted together
items.meaningCN: 聚集的；组装好的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The assembled unit was tested immediately.
items.exampleCN: 组装好的装置立即接受了测试。

items.meaning: the process of gathering or fitting
items.meaningCN: 聚集；装配（-ing 构成动名词或分词）
items.example: Assembling the parts takes patience.
items.exampleCN: 组装这些零件需要耐心。

items.meaning: to take something apart into its parts
items.meaningCN: 拆卸；分解（dis- 表示“分开”）
items.example: You must disassemble the machine to clean it.
items.exampleCN: 必须拆开机器才能清洗。

items.meaning: to assemble again after being taken apart
items.meaningCN: 重新组装（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: He reassembled the engine after the repair.
items.exampleCN: 修理后他重新组装了发动机。

items.meaning: a production line where parts are assembled in sequence
items.meaningCN: 装配线；流水线（assembly + line 复合名词）
items.example: Cars move along the assembly line.
items.exampleCN: 汽车沿装配线移动。

items.meaning: a low-level programming language close to machine code
items.meaningCN: 汇编语言（assembly + language 复合名词）
items.example: The course begins with assembly language.
items.exampleCN: 这门课程从汇编语言开始。

items.meaning: a smaller assembled unit that forms part of a larger one
items.meaningCN: 子组件；分总成（sub- 表示“在下、部分”）
items.example: The wing is a subassembly of the aircraft.
items.exampleCN: 机翼是飞机的一个子组件。

items.meaning: a member of a legislative assembly
items.meaningCN: 议员；议会成员（assembly + man 复合名词）
items.example: The assemblyman voted against the bill.
items.exampleCN: 这位议员投票反对该法案。

latinEntries.meaning: resembling something else
to imitate the appearance or conditions of something
latinEntries.meaningCN: 模拟；模仿（来自 simulare“使相似”）

latinEntries.meaning: to make or become similar; to absorb into a group
happening at the same time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同时发生的（simul“一起”+ tempus“时间”）

definition_en: to judge the value, quality, or amount of something
core_image: 坐在一旁，用量尺给价值或损失定出一个数
scene: 查勘员在受损的房子前拍照、拉卷尺。 The surveyor photographed the damaged house, measured it, and assessed the cost of the repairs.
sceneCN: 这里 assess 是「估价、核定」（第 2 个义项：估算价值或金额）；句意：查勘员拍下受损的房子，量好尺寸，评估了维修费用。

pos.zh: 评估；估价；核定（税额、罚款）；判定

senses.title: Judge the quality of something
senses.titleCN: 评估质量：判断好坏高低
senses.definition: to judge the quality, importance, or ability of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的质量、重要性或能力
senses.example: The committee assessed the proposal carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会仔细评估了这项提案。
senses.why: The judge's assistant once sat beside the judge to fix fines. From 'sit beside and judge' comes the general act of forming a judgment.
senses.whyCN: 法官的助手曾坐在法官旁边核定罚款。从“坐在旁边作判断”产生了“评估”这一一般动作。

senses.title: Estimate value or amount
senses.titleCN: 估价：估算价值或数量
senses.definition: to estimate the value, size, or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 估算某物的价值、规模或数量
senses.example: An expert assessed the painting at two million dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 专家估计这幅画值两百万美元。
senses.why: The legal task was to fix an amount. Assess keeps that numeric branch: look at the thing, then name a figure.
senses.whyCN: 最初的法律任务是确定一个数额。assess 保留了这个数字分支：看对象，然后给出一个数。

senses.title: Fix a tax or fine on someone
senses.titleCN: 核定税额或罚款
senses.definition: to decide how much tax or fine a person or property must pay
senses.definitionCN: 决定某人或某财产应缴多少税或罚款
senses.example: The city assessed the property at a higher rate.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府按更高税率核定了这处房产。
senses.why: This is the sense the word was born in. The Latin verb meant to sit beside a judge, and the first English use was to sit in judgment on how much tax was owed.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最初诞生的义项。拉丁语动词意为“坐在法官旁边”，英语最早的用法就是坐下来裁定该缴多少税。

senses.title: Evaluate a student's work
senses.titleCN: 评定学业：给学生的表现下判断
senses.definition: to judge a student's work or progress, especially for a grade
senses.definitionCN: 评定学生的作业或进步，尤用于评分
senses.example: Teachers assess reading skills at the end of each term.
senses.exampleCN: 教师在每学期末评定阅读能力。
senses.why: A tax amount and a grade are both judgments made by an authority. The educational sense grows from the same act of sitting in judgment.
senses.whyCN: 税额和分数都是权威作出的判断。教育义项从同一个“作判断”的动作长出来。

senses.title: Judge risk or impact
senses.titleCN: 评估风险或影响
senses.definition: to judge how dangerous or serious something is
senses.definitionCN: 判断某事的危险或严重程度
senses.example: Scientists assess the risk of the new chemical.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家评估这种新化学品的风险。
senses.why: Risk is a future amount that cannot be measured directly. Assess estimates it in advance, as a kind of forecast judgment.
senses.whyCN: 风险是无法直接测量的未来量。assess 提前估算它，是一种预测性判断。

senses.title: Evaluate needs or condition
senses.titleCN: 评估需求或状况
senses.definition: to judge what a person needs, especially in health or social care
senses.definitionCN: 判断一个人需要什么，尤用于医疗或社会照护
senses.example: The nurse assessed the patient's condition.
senses.exampleCN: 护士评估了病人的状况。
senses.why: Care begins with a judgment of need. The assessor sits beside the person, observes, and decides what should be done.
senses.whyCN: 照护从对需求的判断开始。评估者坐在当事人旁边，观察并决定该做什么。

senses.title: Assess damages or liability
senses.titleCN: 核定损害赔偿或责任
senses.definition: to decide the amount of damages or responsibility in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中确定损害赔偿或责任的数额
senses.example: The court assessed damages at fifty thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 法院核定了五万英镑的损害赔偿。
senses.why: This is the oldest legal branch: a judge's assistant fixes the sum owed. The word still carries the courtroom image of sitting beside the judge.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的法律分支：法官助手确定应付金额。这个词仍带着“坐在法官旁边”的法庭意象。

senses.title: Judge a situation before acting
senses.titleCN: 研判局势：行动前先判断
senses.definition: to form a judgment of a situation in order to plan an action
senses.definitionCN: 为制定行动而判断形势
senses.example: The officer assessed the crowd before giving orders.
senses.exampleCN: 警官在下令前研判了人群情况。
senses.why: Action needs a reading of the scene. Assess is the pause before movement: observe, judge, then decide.
senses.whyCN: 行动需要先读懂现场。assess 是行动前的停顿：观察、判断，再决定。

intro.en: Assess began as a tax term: a judge's assistant sat beside the judge and fixed the amount owed. From that courtroom image English extended it to any judgment of value.
intro.cn: assess 最初是税务词：法官的助手坐在法官旁边，确定应付金额。英语从这一法庭意象扩展到任何价值判断。

items.en: First recorded as 'to fix the amount of a tax, fine, etc.'
items.cn: 最早记录为“确定税额、罚款等的金额”。

items.en: From Anglo-French assesser, the legal French used in English courts.
items.cn: 来自 Anglo-French assesser，即英国法庭使用的法律法语。

items.en: From Medieval Latin assessare 'fix a tax upon', originally a frequentative of assessus.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 assessare“对……定税”，最初是 assessus 的反复动词。

items.en: assessus is the past participle of assidere 'to sit beside', from ad- 'to' + sedere 'to sit'.
items.cn: assessus 是 assidere“坐在旁边”的过去分词，来自 ad-“向”+ sedere“坐”。

items.en: sedere goes back to PIE *sed- 'to sit', the root behind session, sediment and preside.
items.cn: sedere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *sed-“坐”，session、sediment、preside 都出自这个词根。

items.en: The sense 'estimate the value of property for tax' is from 1809; the general sense 'judge the value of a person or idea' is from 1934.
items.cn: “为征税而估定财产价值”的义项出现于 1809 年；“判断人或想法的价值”的一般义项出现于 1934 年。

note.en: The first group looks and sounds close but has different roots; the second contains other verbs of judging and valuing.
note.cn: 第一组词形或读音接近但词根不同；第二组是其他表示“判断、估价”的动词。

entries.definition: the right or way to enter. It has a hard /k/ sound and comes from 'go toward'.
entries.definitionCN: 进入的权利或通道。它读硬音 /k/，来自“走向”。

entries.definition: a valuable thing or quality. It is a noun and has no verb sense.
entries.definitionCN: 有价值的东西或品质。它是名词，没有动词义。

entries.definition: to state something firmly. It ends in -rt and comes from 'join'.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地陈述。它以 -rt 结尾，来自“连接”。

entries.definition: to help. It comes from 'stand beside', not 'sit beside'.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助。它来自“站在旁边”，不是“坐在旁边”。

entries.definition: to judge the value or quality of something using criteria. It is the most general academic word.
entries.definitionCN: 按标准判断某物的价值或质量。它是最通用的学术词。

entries.definition: to estimate the value of property or an object, especially professionally. It is narrower than assess.
entries.definitionCN: 专业地估算财产或物品价值。它比 assess 更窄。

entries.definition: to calculate an approximate amount. It stresses the number rather than the judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 计算大致数量。它更强调数字，而不是判断。

entries.definition: to form an opinion about someone or something. It is broader and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某事形成看法。它更宽，也不那么技术化。

entries.definition: to give a score or rank to something. It is the usual word for rating performance.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物打分或评级。它是“评定表现”的常用词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- 'to' + sedere 'sit', the *sed- 'sit' family, and the tax/courtroom origin.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad-“向”+ sedere“坐”、*sed-“坐”词族，以及税务/法庭来源。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + sedere 'sit' = 'sit beside'. The judge's assistant sat beside the judge to fix the tax or fine.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ sedere“坐”=“坐在旁边”。法官助手坐在法官旁边核定税额或罚款。

normal.en: Session, sediment and preside share the same *sed- 'sit' root: a session is a sitting, sediment settles, a president sits before.
normal.cn: session、sediment、preside 共享 *sed-“坐”词根：session 是一次坐会，sediment 沉淀，president 坐在前面。

normal.en: Assessment is the noun: the act of sitting beside and judging, or the judgment produced.
normal.cn: assessment 是名词：坐在旁边判断的行为，或产生的判断。

normal.en: An assessor is the person who assesses; in insurance and tax, the official who fixes the amount.
normal.cn: assessor 是评估者；在保险和税务中，指核定金额的官员。

normal.en: Assess the damage is the everyday phrase: look at the broken thing and name what it will cost.
normal.cn: assess the damage 是日常短语：看看损坏的东西，说出要花多少钱。

abstract.en: Abstractly, assess is a judgment performed from beside the object: you do not become the thing, you sit next to it and set a value.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，assess 是从对象旁边作出的判断：你不变成那个东西，而是坐在它旁边给它定值。

abstract.en: The value can be money (tax, damages), quality (work), risk (future harm), or need (care).
abstract.cn: 这个值可以是金钱（税、损害赔偿）、质量（作品）、风险（未来伤害）或需求（照护）。

abstract.en: So the courtroom image survives in every sense: a person at the side, a standard, and a number or verdict that follows.
abstract.cn: 所以法庭意象在每个义项中都存活：旁边的人、一把标准尺，以及随之而来的数字或裁决。

examples.en: We need to assess the damage before we repair the roof.
examples.cn: 修屋顶前我们需要评估损坏情况。

examples.en: The teacher assesses each student's speaking ability.
examples.cn: 老师评估每个学生的口语能力。

examples.en: The government assessed a new tax on imported cars.
examples.cn: 政府对进口汽车核定了新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿塞斯”——阿塞斯坐在房子旁边，量一量、算一算维修费 → assess 评估、估价

root: 拉丁语 assidere“坐在旁边”（ad- + sedere），原指法官助手坐在旁边核定税额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of assess, all built on one courtroom image: someone sits beside the object, applies a standard, and fixes a value. The value may be quality, money, a tax, a grade, risk, need, damages, or a plan of action.
sensesIntro.cn: assess 的八个义项都建立在一个法庭意象上：某人坐在对象旁边，适用一把标准尺，定出一个值。这个值可以是质量、金钱、税额、分数、风险、需求、损害赔偿或行动方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a judge's assistant sits beside the judge and fixes an amount.
core.cn: 核心意象：法官的助手坐在法官旁边，核定一个数额。

branches.en: JUDGMENT AND VALUE: a general opinion of quality, or a specific estimated amount.
branches.cn: 判断与价值：对质量的一般看法，或估算出的具体金额。

branches.en: TAX: an authority fixes what must be paid.
branches.cn: 税：权威机构核定应缴多少。

branches.en: EDUCATION AND RISK: a grade is a judgment; risk is a judgment about the future.
branches.cn: 教育与风险：分数是一种判断；风险是对未来的判断。

branches.en: CARE: a professional judges a person's needs or condition.
branches.cn: 照护：专业人员判断一个人的需求或状况。

branches.en: LEGAL AND TACTICAL: damages are fixed in court; a situation is read before action.
branches.cn: 法律与战术：在法庭上核定损害赔偿；行动前先研判局势。

intro.en: English builds assessment, assessor, assessable, reassess and several compounds from assess. The -ment, -or and -able suffixes are the productive parts.
intro.cn: 英语由 assess 构成 assessment、assessor、assessable、reassess 及若干复合词。-ment、-or、-able 是能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on sedere 'to sit' (PIE *sed-): session, sediment, preside and reside all describe someone or something sitting or settling.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 sedere“坐”（原始印欧语 *sed-）上：session、sediment、preside、reside 都描述某人或某物坐着或沉降。

items.meaning: the act of judging, or the judgment made
items.meaningCN: 评估；估价；核定（-ment 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The assessment will take two weeks.
items.exampleCN: 评估需要两周。

items.meaning: a person who assesses, especially for tax or insurance
items.meaningCN: 评估员；估税员（-or 表示做动作的人）
items.example: The assessor measured the damaged wall.
items.exampleCN: 评估员测量了受损的墙。

items.meaning: able to be assessed or taxed
items.meaningCN: 可评估的；应课税的（-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: The income is assessable for tax.
items.exampleCN: 这笔收入应课税。

items.meaning: to assess again
items.meaningCN: 重新评估（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: We must reassess the plan after the results.
items.exampleCN: 结果出来后我们必须重新评估计划。

items.meaning: a second assessment
items.meaningCN: 重新评估（re- + assess + -ment）
items.example: The case needs a full reassessment.
items.exampleCN: 这个案件需要全面重新评估。

items.meaning: the act of judging one's own work or tax
items.meaningCN: 自我评估；自行申报（self- + assess + -ment）
items.example: Students complete a self-assessment at the end.
items.exampleCN: 学生在最后完成自我评估。

items.meaning: a formal judgment of possible danger
items.meaningCN: 风险评估（risk + assessment 复合名词）
items.example: A risk assessment is required before the climb.
items.exampleCN: 攀登前必须进行风险评估。

items.meaning: a person whose property or income is assessed
items.meaningCN: 被评估者；纳税人（-ee 表示受影响的人）
items.example: The assessee may appeal the decision.
items.exampleCN: 被评估者可以对该决定提出上诉。

items.meaning: the process of judging or valuing
items.meaningCN: 评估中的；评估过程（-ing 构成分词或动名词）
items.example: The assessing officer visited the site.
items.exampleCN: 评估官员访问了现场。

items.meaning: not yet assessed
items.meaningCN: 未评估的；未核定的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: The unassessed properties were listed separately.
items.exampleCN: 未评估的房产被单独列出。

latinEntries.meaning: a period of sitting together for business
material that settles at the bottom of a liquid
to sit before others as the person in charge
to live in a place, literally to remain sitting there

definition_en: to give a task, role, place, or cause to someone or something
core_image: 把写有名字和用途的标签，贴到人或物上
scene: 主管拿着项目文件站在任务板前。 The supervisor assigned the new project to the youngest designer and wrote her name on the task board.
sceneCN: 这里 assign 是「指派任务」（第 1 个义项：把任务分给某人）；句意：主管把新项目指派给最年轻的设计师，并在任务板上写下她的名字。

pos.zh: 分配；指派；指定；把……归因于

senses.title: Give a task or duty to someone
senses.titleCN: 分配任务：把工作交到某人手上
senses.definition: to give someone a particular job or duty
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作或职责交给某人
senses.example: The editor assigned the interview to a young reporter.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把这次采访分配给了年轻记者。
senses.why: Latin ad- 'to' + signare 'mark' means 'mark something to someone'. A task is marked with a person's name, so it becomes that person's job.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad-“向”+ signare“标记”意为“把某物标记给某人”。任务被标上某人的名字，于是成了那个人的工作。

senses.title: Allot a share or resource
senses.titleCN: 分配资源：把份额划给某人
senses.definition: to give a particular amount or share of something to someone
senses.definitionCN: 把一定数量或份额给某人
senses.example: Each team was assigned a budget of ten thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 每个团队分到一万美元预算。
senses.why: A share is also marked off and handed over. Assign treats money, time and materials as portions that can be labelled and allotted.
senses.whyCN: 份额同样是被划出来并交出去的。assign 把钱、时间和材料看作可以贴标签并分配的份额。

senses.title: Appoint someone to a role
senses.titleCN: 指派职位：把某人放到一个位置上
senses.definition: to appoint someone to a position or role
senses.definitionCN: 把某人任命到某个职位或角色
senses.example: She was assigned to the role of project leader.
senses.exampleCN: 她被指派担任项目负责人。
senses.why: A person can be marked for a post, just as a task is marked for a person. The word moves from the work to the office that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 人可以像任务一样被标记到一个岗位上。这个词从工作本身移到承载工作的职位。

senses.title: Fix a time or value
senses.titleCN: 指定时间或数值：定下一个标准
senses.definition: to set a particular time, date, or value for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事设定具体时间、日期或数值
senses.example: The court assigned a date for the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 法院指定了听证日期。
senses.why: An assigned date is a date marked out from all possible dates. The core act is still selection by marking.
senses.whyCN: 指定的日期是从所有可能日期中被标出的那一天。核心动作仍是“通过标记来选定”。

senses.title: Ascribe a cause or blame
senses.titleCN: 归因：把原因或责任贴到某人身上
senses.definition: to say that something is caused by or belongs to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 说某事由某人或某物引起，或属于其
senses.example: They assigned the failure to poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把失败归因于计划不周。
senses.why: Here the label is a cause. Assign puts the cause on a person or factor, just as it puts a task on a worker.
senses.whyCN: 这里的标签是原因。assign 把原因贴到某个人或因素上，正如把任务贴到工人身上。

senses.title: Designate a place or use
senses.titleCN: 指定用途或位置：划给某个用途
senses.definition: to set something aside for a particular use or place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物留作特定用途或放在特定位置
senses.example: These seats are assigned to guests.
senses.exampleCN: 这些座位是留给客人的。
senses.why: A seat can carry a name or a category. Assign marks who may use it, turning an open seat into a designated one.
senses.whyCN: 座位可以带名字或类别。assign 标出谁可以使用它，把空座变成指定座位。

senses.title: Transfer a legal right
senses.titleCN: 法律转让：把权利正式转给他人
senses.definition: to transfer a right, property, or interest to another person by law
senses.definitionCN: 依法把权利、财产或权益转给他人
senses.example: The seller assigned the lease to the new tenant.
senses.exampleCN: 卖方把租约转让给了新租户。
senses.why: In law, a right is marked as belonging to a new holder. The document records the transfer, and the right is assigned.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，权利被标记为属于新的持有人。文件记录这次转移，这项权利就被 assign 了。

senses.title: Give a value to a variable
senses.titleCN: 计算机赋值：把值写进变量
senses.definition: to give a value to a variable in a computer program
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机程序中给变量一个值
senses.example: The program assigns zero to the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把计数器赋值为零。
senses.why: A variable is an empty slot with a name. Assign puts a value into that named slot, exactly the old image of marking and giving.
senses.whyCN: 变量是一个带名字的空槽。assign 把值放进这个有名字的槽，正是古老的“标记并给予”意象。

senses.title: Attach a meaning or significance
senses.titleCN: 赋予意义：把含义贴到符号上
senses.definition: to give a particular meaning or significance to something
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某物特定含义或重要性
senses.example: Philosophers ask how words are assigned meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问词语如何被赋予意义。
senses.why: Meaning is treated as something that can be attached to a symbol. Assign names the act of fixing which meaning belongs to which form.
senses.whyCN: 意义被看作可以附到符号上的东西。assign 指固定“哪个意义属于哪个形式”的动作。

intro.en: Assign began as a legal and administrative verb: something is marked out and given to a person. The 'mark' root survives in sign, signature and design.
intro.cn: assign 最初是法律和行政动词：某物被标出并交给某人。“标记”词根保留在 sign、signature、design 中。

items.en: First recorded in English, meaning 'to allot, assign, appoint' and also 'to transfer by law'.
items.cn: 最早记录于约 1300 年，意为“分配、指派、任命”，也有“依法转让”之义。

items.en: From Old French assigner 'assign, allot, set (a date); appoint' (12c.), Modern French assigner.
items.cn: 来自古法语 assigner“分配、划给、确定（日期）；任命”（12 世纪），现代法语作 assigner。

items.en: From Latin assignare/adsignare 'to mark out to, assign, allot, bestow; give as a mark to'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 assignare/adsignare“标给、分配、授予；作为标记给予”。

items.en: assignare = ad- 'to' + signare 'to mark, sign', from signum 'a mark, sign, token'.
items.cn: assignare = ad-“向”+ signare“标记、签名”，后者来自 signum“记号、标志”。

items.en: Modern English adds the computing sense 'give a value to a variable' in the 20th century. Assignment is the noun for both a task and a legal transfer.
items.cn: 现代英语在 20 世纪增加了计算机义“给变量赋值”。名词 assignment 既指任务，也指法律转让。

note.en: The first group looks close in spelling; the second contains other verbs of giving and allocating.
note.cn: 第一组拼写接近；第二组是其他表示“给予、分配”的动词。

entries.definition: to suppose or take on. It shares the ass- opening but not the 'mark' root.
entries.definitionCN: 假定；承担。它同样以 ass- 开头，但没有“标记”词根。

entries.definition: to judge value. It comes from 'sit beside', not from 'mark'.
entries.definitionCN: 评估价值。它来自“坐在旁边”，不是“标记”。

entries.definition: to help. It comes from 'stand beside', another root.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助。它来自“站在旁边”，又是另一个词根。

entries.definition: to agree or approve. It comes from 'feel with', not from 'mark'.
entries.definitionCN: 同意；赞成。它来自“共同感受”，不是“标记”。

entries.definition: to give a share of money, time, or space for a purpose. It is close to assign but more financial and planning-oriented.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的分配金钱、时间或空间。它接近 assign，但更偏财务与规划。

entries.definition: to give a fixed share to someone. It stresses the portion rather than the name or role.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人固定的一份。它更强调份额，而不是名字或角色。

entries.definition: to choose someone for an official position. It is narrower than assign and usually formal.
entries.definitionCN: 选某人担任正式职位。它比 assign 窄，通常更正式。

entries.definition: to say that something is caused by or belongs to someone. It overlaps with assign in the 'blame' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 说某事由某人引起或属于某人。它在“归咎”义上与 assign 重叠。

entries.definition: to mark or name something for a purpose. It stresses the official label more than the giving.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的标记或命名某物。它比“给予”更强调官方标签。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- 'to' + signare 'mark', the sign/signature family, and the legal transfer sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad-“向”+ signare“标记”、sign/signature 词族，以及法律转让义。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + signare 'mark' = 'mark to'. Assigning a task is marking it with someone's name.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ signare“标记”=“标记给”。分配任务就是给它标上某人的名字。

normal.en: Sign, signal, signature and design all come from signum 'mark': a sign marks something, and assignment marks who gets what.
normal.cn: sign、signal、signature、design 都来自 signum“标记”：符号标记事物，分配则标记谁得到什么。

normal.en: An assignment is both a piece of work and a legal transfer. The same noun covers schoolwork and property rights.
normal.cn: assignment 既是作业，也是法律转让。同一个名词覆盖学业任务和财产权利。

normal.en: In computing, x = 5 assigns the value 5 to the variable x: a value is marked onto a name.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，x = 5 把值 5 赋给变量 x：一个值被标记到一个名字上。

normal.en: Assign blame is the everyday phrase for putting responsibility on someone, like sticking a label on a person.
normal.cn: assign blame 是把责任贴到某人身上的日常说法，像给人贴标签。

abstract.en: Abstractly, assign is a labelling operation: take an unowned task, share, role, date or cause, and attach an owner to it.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，assign 是一种贴标签操作：拿一个无主的任务、份额、角色、日期或原因，给它附上一个主人。

abstract.en: The operation always has two sides: the thing marked and the person or slot to which it is marked.
abstract.cn: 这个操作总有两边：被标记的东西，以及它被标记到的人或槽位。

abstract.en: So assign underlies work allocation, legal transfer and even variable binding: in each case, a mark creates a relation of belonging.
abstract.cn: 所以 assign 支撑着工作分配、法律转让，甚至变量绑定：每种情况下，标记都创造出一种归属关系。

examples.en: The teacher assigned a short essay to each group.
examples.cn: 老师给每个小组布置了一篇短文。

examples.en: Please assign the new employee to the marketing team.
examples.cn: 请把新员工分配到市场团队。

examples.en: She assigned her late arrival to the heavy traffic.
examples.cn: 她把自己的迟到归因于交通拥堵。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿赛恩”——阿赛恩在任务板上写下名字，把工作分给每个人 → assign 分配、指派

root: 拉丁语 assignare = ad-“向”+ signare“标记”，核心是“标出并给予”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of assign, all built on one act: mark a thing and give it to a person, place, or slot. The thing may be a task, a share, a role, a date, a cause, a seat, a legal right, a variable value, or a meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: assign 的九个义项都建立在一个动作上：标记某物，并把它交给某人、某处或某个槽位。这个物可以是任务、份额、角色、日期、原因、座位、法律权利、变量值或意义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label is written with a name and stuck onto a thing, making it belong to that name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写有名字的标签被贴到某物上，使该物属于这个名字。

branches.en: WORK AND ROLE: a task or an office is marked with a person's name.
branches.cn: 工作与角色：任务或职位被标上某人的名字。

branches.en: SHARE AND DATE: a portion or a date is marked out from a larger set.
branches.cn: 份额与日期：一份资源或一个日期从更大的集合中被划出。

branches.en: CAUSE AND MEANING: a cause or a meaning is attached to a person, factor or symbol.
branches.cn: 原因与意义：原因或意义被附到某人、某因素或符号上。

branches.en: PLACE: a seat or place is designated for a particular user.
branches.cn: 位置：座位或地点被指定给特定使用者。

branches.en: FORMAL AND TECHNICAL: a legal right is transferred; a value is bound to a variable.
branches.cn: 正式与技术：法律权利被转让；值被绑定到变量。

intro.en: Assign builds assignment, assignee, assignor, assignable and reassign. The -ment, -ee, -or and -able suffixes mark result, receiver, giver and possibility.
intro.cn: assign 构成 assignment、assignee、assignor、assignable、reassign。-ment、-ee、-or、-able 分别标出结果、接受者、给予者和可能性。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on signum 'mark, sign': sign, signal, signature and design all involve making or reading a mark.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 signum“记号、标志”上：sign、signal、signature、design 都涉及留下或读取标记。

items.meaning: a task given to someone, or the act of giving it
items.meaningCN: 任务；作业；分配（-ment 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The assignment is due on Friday.
items.exampleCN: 作业周五到期。

items.meaning: a person to whom a task, right, or property is assigned
items.meaningCN: 受让人；被指派者（-ee 表示接受者）
items.example: The assignee signed the transfer document.
items.exampleCN: 受让人签署了转让文件。

items.meaning: a person who assigns a right or property
items.meaningCN: 转让人；分配者（-or 表示给予者）
items.example: The assignor retains no claim to the lease.
items.exampleCN: 转让人不再对租约享有权利。

items.meaning: able to be assigned or transferred
items.meaningCN: 可分配的；可转让的（-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: The contract is freely assignable.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同可以自由转让。

items.meaning: to assign again or to a different person
items.meaningCN: 重新分配；改派（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: The manager reassigned the case to another lawyer.
items.exampleCN: 经理把案件改派给另一位律师。

items.meaning: a second or different assignment
items.meaningCN: 重新分配；改派（re- + assign + -ment）
items.example: The reassignment took effect on Monday.
items.exampleCN: 改派在周一生效。

items.meaning: not given to anyone
items.meaningCN: 未分配的；未指派的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: The unassigned seats are at the back.
items.exampleCN: 未分配的座位在后面。

items.meaning: given or fixed by an authority
items.meaningCN: 被分配的；指定的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: Students must sit in their assigned seats.
items.exampleCN: 学生必须坐在指定座位上。

items.meaning: a piece of schoolwork given to students
items.meaningCN: 家庭作业（homework + assignment 复合名词）
items.example: The homework assignment covers two chapters.
items.exampleCN: 家庭作业涵盖两章。

items.meaning: the act or result of giving tasks to people
items.meaningCN: 任务分配（task + assignment 复合名词）
items.example: Task assignment is handled by the team leader.
items.exampleCN: 任务分配由组长负责。

latinEntries.meaning: a mark or object that stands for something
latinEntries.meaningCN: 符号；标志（来自 signum“记号”）

latinEntries.meaning: a sign that conveys information
a person's written name used as a mark
to mark out a plan or structure

definition_en: to help someone do something, or an act of help
core_image: 站在需要帮助的人身旁，分担一部分重量
scene: 球场上，队友把球传向门前的前锋。 The teammate passed the ball to the striker to assist her in scoring the goal.
sceneCN: 这里 assist 是「助攻」（第 4 个义项：体育中帮助队友得分）；句意：队友把球传给前锋，助攻她完成进球。

senses.title: Help someone do something
senses.titleCN: 帮助：在某人做事时搭一把手
senses.definition: to help someone perform a task
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人完成一项任务
senses.example: A nurse assisted the doctor during the examination.
senses.exampleCN: 检查时一名护士协助医生。
senses.why: Latin assistere is 'to stand by'. Help begins with presence: you take a stand next to the person who needs you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 assistere 是“站在旁边”。帮助从在场开始：你站到需要你的人身旁。

senses.title: Help in an official or professional capacity
senses.titleCN: 职务协助：以官方或专业身份帮忙
senses.definition: to help in an official role, especially police, medical or legal work
senses.definitionCN: 以官方角色提供帮助，尤指警务、医疗或法律工作
senses.example: The local officer assisted the federal investigators.
senses.exampleCN: 当地警官协助联邦调查人员。
senses.why: The stand-by sense becomes institutional: an assistant stands beside an official and supports the official's work.
senses.whyCN: “站在旁边”变成制度性的：助理站在官员身旁，支持其工作。

senses.title: Facilitate a process
senses.titleCN: 辅助过程：帮助某事顺利进行
senses.definition: to make a process easier or help it work
senses.definitionCN: 使过程更容易或帮助其运转
senses.example: The software assists users in finding the right file.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件帮助用户找到正确的文件。
senses.why: A tool can stand beside a task and carry part of the load. The helper need not be a person; anything that supports the process can assist.
senses.whyCN: 工具可以站在任务旁边，承担一部分负荷。帮助者不必是人；任何支持过程的东西都可以 assist。

senses.title: A sports assist
senses.titleCN: 体育助攻：帮助队友得分
senses.definition: to make the pass or play that leads directly to a score
senses.definitionCN: 做出直接导致得分的传球或配合
senses.example: She assisted the winning goal with a low cross.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一记低平传中助攻了制胜球。
senses.why: In sport, standing beside a scorer means giving the final pass. The helper gets a recorded share in the score.
senses.whyCN: 在体育中，站在得分者旁边意味着送出最后一传。帮助者在得分记录里分到一份。

senses.title: Medical assistance
senses.titleCN: 医疗辅助：在治疗中协助
senses.definition: to help in medical treatment or care
senses.definitionCN: 在治疗或照护中提供帮助
senses.example: The team assisted the surgeon throughout the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在整个手术中协助外科医生。
senses.why: A medical team stands beside the lead doctor. Assist describes the supporting role, not the decision-making role.
senses.whyCN: 医疗团队站在主刀医生身旁。assist 描述的是支持角色，而不是决策角色。

senses.title: Assist someone to do something
senses.titleCN: 协助某人做某事：正式用法
senses.definition: to help someone to do something; formal, often with to
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人做某事；正式用法，常接 to
senses.example: The guide assisted us to cross the river safely.
senses.exampleCN: 向导协助我们安全过河。
senses.why: This formal pattern makes the helper an enabler: the other person still acts, but with support from beside.
senses.whyCN: 这个正式句式把帮助者变成促成者：对方仍然行动，但旁边有人支撑。

senses.title: An act of assistance
senses.titleCN: 援助行为：一次帮助
senses.definition: a single act of help, especially in sports statistics
senses.definitionCN: 一次帮助行为，尤指体育统计
senses.example: He recorded two assists in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛中记录了两次助攻。
