senses.why: The noun turns the supporting act into a countable object. A team can count how many times someone stood beside a scorer.
senses.whyCN: 名词把支持行为变成可计数的对象。球队可以数出某人多少次站在得分者身旁。

senses.title: Assist at a ceremony or birth
senses.titleCN: 在场协助：在仪式或分娩现场帮忙
senses.definition: to be present and help at a ceremony or birth; formal
senses.definitionCN: 在仪式或分娩现场出席并提供帮助；正式用法
senses.example: The midwife assisted at the birth.
senses.exampleCN: 助产士在分娩时协助。
senses.why: Some helping is defined by presence at an event. To assist at a birth is to stand by and support the process as it happens.
senses.whyCN: 有些帮助由“在事件现场”定义。assist at a birth 就是站在旁边，在过程发生时提供支持。

intro.en: Assist is built on the Latin verb 'to stand'. The helper stands beside the person in need, and the noun later becomes a countable act, including a sports statistic.
intro.cn: assist 建立在拉丁语“站”的动词上。帮助者站在需要的人旁边；名词后来变成可数的行为，包括体育统计。

items.en: First recorded as assisten 'to help, aid, give assistance or support to in some undertaking or effort'.
items.cn: 最早记录为 assisten“帮助、援助、在某项事业或努力中给予支持”。

items.en: From Old French assister 'to stand by, help, put, place, assist' (14c.), Modern French assister.
items.cn: 来自古法语 assister“站在旁边、帮助、放置、协助”（14 世纪），现代法语 assister。

items.en: From Latin assistere 'stand by, take a stand near, attend', from ad- 'to' + sistere 'stand still, take a stand'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 assistere“站在旁边、靠近站立、出席”，由 ad-“向”+ sistere“站住、立定”构成。

items.en: sistere is a reduplicated form of the root *sta- 'to stand, make or be firm'.
items.cn: sistere 是词根 *sta-“站立、使坚固”的叠词形式。

items.en: The noun assist is recorded from the 1570s; the sporting sense appears in baseball in 1877 and in ice hockey in 1925.
items.cn: 名词 assist 记录于 16 世纪 70 年代；体育义在棒球中见于 1877 年，在冰球中见于 1925 年。

note.en: The first group is about the -sist family and similar spellings; the second is about other words for help.
note.cn: 第一组看 -sist 词族和相似拼写；第二组看其他表示“帮助”的词。

entries.definition: to demand something firmly. in- 'on' + sistere 'stand' gives 'stand on' a point.
entries.definitionCN: 坚决要求。in-“在……上”+ sistere“站”即“站在某点上”。

entries.definition: to be made up of. con- 'together' + sistere 'stand' gives 'stand together'.
entries.definitionCN: 由……组成。con-“一起”+ sistere“站”即“站在一起”。

entries.definition: to oppose or withstand. re- 'against' + sistere 'stand' gives 'stand against'.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗；反抗。re-“反”+ sistere“站”即“站在对面”。

entries.definition: to judge value. It comes from 'sit beside', not 'stand beside'.
entries.definitionCN: 评估价值。它来自“坐在旁边”，不是“站在旁边”。

entries.definition: to make it easier for someone to do something. It is the broadest and most everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人做事更容易。它是最宽、最日常的词。

entries.definition: to help, especially in an urgent or official situation. It is often used of medical or humanitarian aid.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助，尤指紧急或官方场合。常用于医疗或人道援助。

entries.definition: to hold up or help someone over time. It stresses sustained backing rather than a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑；长期帮助。它强调持续支持，而不是一次行为。

entries.definition: to make a process easier. It is more formal and usually takes an action or process as its object.
entries.definitionCN: 使过程更容易。它更正式，通常以行动或过程为宾语。

entries.definition: to support someone, especially in an argument or task. It is informal and often used with people.
entries.definitionCN: 支持某人，尤指在争论或任务中。它较口语化，常与人搭配。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- 'to' + sistere 'stand', the -sist family, and the sports statistic.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad-“向”+ sistere“站”、-sist 词族，以及体育统计义。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + sistere 'stand' = 'stand beside'. Assist begins with taking a stand next to someone who needs help.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ sistere“站”=“站在旁边”。assist 从站到需要帮助的人身旁开始。

normal.en: Insist, consist, resist and assist all contain sistere 'stand': stand on, stand together, stand against, stand beside.
normal.cn: insist、consist、resist、assist 都含 sistere“站”：站在某点上、站在一起、站在对面、站在旁边。

normal.en: An assistant is literally one who stands by; assistance is the act of standing by.
normal.cn: assistant 字面就是“站在旁边的人”；assistance 是“站在旁边”的行为。

normal.en: In football, an assist is the pass that lets a teammate score: you stand beside the scorer in the record.
normal.cn: 在足球中，assist 是让队友得分的传球：你在记录里站到了得分者旁边。

normal.en: Assistive technology is real: devices that stand beside a person and support a task.
normal.cn: assistive technology 是真实说法：站在人旁边、支持某项任务的设备。

abstract.en: Abstractly, assist is support from beside: the main actor still acts, but another presence carries part of the difficulty.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，assist 是来自旁边的支持：主要行动者仍在行动，但另一个存在分担了一部分困难。

abstract.en: The support can be physical, official, procedural, statistical or technological; the geometry is always 'standing beside'.
abstract.cn: 支持可以是身体的、职务的、程序的、统计的或技术的；几何关系始终是“站在旁边”。

abstract.en: So assist does not mean taking over. It means reducing the load of the person who is still doing the work.
abstract.cn: 所以 assist 不意味着接管，而是减轻那个仍在做事的人的负担。

examples.en: A volunteer assisted the elderly man across the street.
examples.cn: 一名志愿者帮助那位老人过马路。

examples.en: The app assists students in organizing their notes.
examples.cn: 这个应用帮助学生整理笔记。

examples.en: She gave two assists in the final match.
examples.cn: 她在决赛中送出两次助攻。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿西斯”——阿西斯站在队友旁边，一脚传球帮他进球 → assist 帮助、助攻

root: 拉丁语 assistere“站在旁边”（ad- + sistere“站”），核心是“站到需要的人身旁”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of assist, all built on one posture: standing beside someone who is doing the work. The standing can be practical help, official support, a tool's facilitation, a sports pass, medical backup, formal enabling, a counted act, or presence at a birth.
sensesIntro.cn: assist 的八个义项都建立在一个姿势上：站在正在做事的人旁边。这个“站”可以是实际帮忙、职务支持、工具辅助、体育传球、医疗后援、正式促成、一次被计数的行为，或分娩时的在场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a helper takes a stand beside the person who carries the main task.
core.cn: 核心意象：帮助者站到承担主要任务的人旁边。

branches.en: DIRECT HELP: a person stands beside another and helps with the task.
branches.cn: 直接帮助：一个人站到另一个人旁边，帮他完成当前任务。

branches.en: OFFICIAL PRESENCE: professional, medical and ceremonial help is defined by standing by in a role.
branches.cn: 职务在场：专业、医疗和仪式协助由“以某种角色站在旁边”来定义。

branches.en: TOOL SUPPORT: a device or process stands beside a task and makes it easier.
branches.cn: 工具支持：设备或流程站在任务旁边，使它更容易完成。

branches.en: SPORTS: the final pass is help that is counted as a share in the score.
branches.cn: 体育：最后一传是一种帮助，并在得分记录中占一份。

branches.en: NOUN: the act of standing by becomes a countable item, especially in statistics.
branches.cn: 名词：站在旁边的行为变成可计数的项目，尤用于统计。

intro.en: Assist builds assistance, assistant, assistive and the negative unassisted. The -ance, -ant and -ive suffixes are the productive parts.
intro.cn: assist 构成 assistance、assistant、assistive 和否定形式 unassisted。-ance、-ant、-ive 是能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on sistere 'to stand' (PIE *sta-): insist, consist, resist and exist all describe a way of standing.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 sistere“站”（原始印欧语 *sta-）上：insist、consist、resist、exist 都描述某种“站”的方式。

items.meaning: the act of helping, or the help given
items.meaningCN: 帮助；援助（-ance 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: The project needs financial assistance.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目需要财政援助。

items.meaning: a person who helps another, especially at work
items.meaningCN: 助手；助理（-ant 表示做动作的人）
items.example: The assistant answered the phone.
items.exampleCN: 助理接了电话。

items.meaning: designed to help someone perform a task
items.meaningCN: 辅助性的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Assistive devices help people with limited mobility.
items.exampleCN: 辅助设备帮助行动不便的人。

items.meaning: done without help
items.meaningCN: 无协助的；独立的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: He climbed the wall unassisted.
items.exampleCN: 他独自爬上了墙。

items.meaning: given help; supported
items.meaningCN: 受协助的；辅助的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The assisted living centre provides daily care.
items.exampleCN: 辅助生活中心提供日常照护。

items.meaning: the act of helping
items.meaningCN: 帮助中的；协助行为（-ing 构成分词或动名词）
items.example: She is assisting with the survey.
items.exampleCN: 她正在协助调查。

items.meaning: devices or software that help people perform tasks
items.meaningCN: 辅助技术（assistive + technology 复合名词）
items.example: Assistive technology can read text aloud.
items.exampleCN: 辅助技术可以把文本朗读出来。

items.meaning: a person who helps a teacher in a classroom
items.meaningCN: 助教（teaching + assistant 复合名词）
items.example: The teaching assistant marked the quizzes.
items.exampleCN: 助教批改了测验。

items.meaning: a dog trained to help a person with a disability
items.meaningCN: 辅助犬（assist + dog 复合名词）
items.example: An assist dog can open doors for its owner.
items.exampleCN: 辅助犬能为主人开门。

items.meaning: the count of assists in a game
items.meaningCN: 助攻数（assist + score 复合名词）
items.example: His assist score led the league.
items.exampleCN: 他的助攻数领跑联赛。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand firmly on a demand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 坚持；坚决要求（in-“在……上”+ sistere“站”）

latinEntries.meaning: to stand together as parts of a whole
to stand against something
to stand out, hence to be present
latinEntries.meaningCN: 存在（ex-“出”+ sistere“站”，即“站出来”）

definition_en: to take something as true, or to take on a role, quality, or appearance
core_image: 把一件本不属于自己的东西拿起来，放到自己身上
scene: 新经理走进办公室，桌上放着一份没人签过的责任清单。 The new manager assumed all responsibility for the department, even though no one had formally handed it to her.
sceneCN: 这里 assume 是「承担」（第 2 个义项：把责任接到自己身上）；句意：新经理承担了部门的全部责任，尽管没有人正式把这份责任交给她。

pos.zh: 假定；承担；就任；装作；呈现

senses.title: Suppose something is true
senses.titleCN: 假定：没有证据也先当作真的
senses.definition: to accept something as true before there is proof
senses.definitionCN: 在没有证据之前就先接受某事为真
senses.example: I assume you have read the report.
senses.exampleCN: 我假定你已经读过报告。
senses.why: Latin assumere means 'to take up'. A supposition is taken up into the mind and held as if it were true, even without proof.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 assumere 意为“拿起来”。一个假定被拿进头脑，并被当作真的持有，即使没有证据。

senses.title: Take on a duty or responsibility
senses.titleCN: 承担：把责任接到自己身上
senses.definition: to take on a duty, role, or responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 承担职责、角色或责任
senses.example: She assumed responsibility for the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 她承担了整个部门的责任。
senses.why: Responsibility is a burden lying elsewhere. To assume it is to lift that burden and place it on oneself.
senses.whyCN: 责任是放在别处的重担。assume 它，就是把那副担子拿起来，放到自己身上。

senses.title: Take power or control
senses.titleCN: 夺取控制权：把权力拿过来
senses.definition: to take control or power, sometimes without the right to do so
senses.definitionCN: 取得控制或权力，有时并无正当权利
senses.example: The army assumed control of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 军队控制了这座城市。
senses.why: Power is another thing that can be lifted. When no one formally hands it over, assume carries a hint of seizing or arrogating.
senses.whyCN: 权力也是可以被拿起来的东西。当无人正式移交时，assume 带有一丝“夺取、僭取”的意味。

senses.title: Put on a false appearance
senses.titleCN: 装作：戴上一副假面孔
senses.definition: to pretend to have a feeling or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 假装拥有某种感受或外表
senses.example: He assumed an air of confidence before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前他装出一副自信的样子。
senses.why: An appearance can be put on like clothing. The person takes up a mask and wears it, even if the inner state is different.
senses.whyCN: 外表可以像衣服一样穿上。人拿起一副面具戴上，即使内心状态并不相同。

senses.title: Begin to have a quality
senses.titleCN: 呈现：开始具有某种性质
senses.definition: to begin to show a particular quality or form
senses.definitionCN: 开始显示某种性质或形态
senses.example: The problem assumed a new urgency after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，问题呈现出新的紧迫性。
senses.why: A situation can take up a new shape. Here assume is intransitive in feel: the thing itself puts on a new quality.
senses.whyCN: 情况可以拿起一个新的形状。这里的 assume 感觉上是不及物的：事物本身披上一种新性质。

senses.title: Take a premise in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑假定：把命题当作前提
senses.definition: to accept a proposition as a premise for argument
senses.definitionCN: 接受一个命题作为论证前提
senses.example: Assume that all men are mortal, then Socrates is mortal.
senses.exampleCN: 假定所有人都会死，那么苏格拉底会死。
senses.why: Logic explicitly takes a proposition up and places it at the base of a proof. The assumption is a starting point held without proof.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑明确地拿起一个命题，把它放在证明的底部。假定就是一个无需证明而持有的起点。

senses.title: The Assumption in theology
senses.titleCN: 宗教中的“圣母升天”
senses.definition: the reception of the Virgin Mary into heaven; a historical theological sense
senses.definitionCN: 圣母马利亚被接升天；历史上的神学义
senses.example: The Feast of the Assumption is celebrated in August.
senses.exampleCN: 圣母升天节在八月庆祝。
senses.why: The Latin past participle assumptus means 'taken up'. Theology uses assume literally: a person is taken up into heaven.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语过去分词 assumptus 意为“被拿起”。神学按字面使用 assume：人被接升上天。

senses.title: Take over a debt or risk
senses.titleCN: 承接债务或风险：把责任接过来
senses.definition: to take over a debt, risk, or obligation from someone else
senses.definitionCN: 从他人手中接过债务、风险或义务
senses.example: The buyer assumed the mortgage with the house.
senses.exampleCN: 买方随房子承接了抵押贷款。
senses.why: A debt can be transferred by taking it onto oneself. In finance, assume is the precise word for taking over another's obligation.
senses.whyCN: 债务可以通过“接到自己身上”而转移。在金融中，assume 是“承接他人义务”的准确用词。

senses.title: Arrogate a right or authority
senses.titleCN: 僭取权利：把不属于自己的权利拿过来
senses.definition: to take a right or authority for oneself without being granted it
senses.definitionCN: 未经授予就把权利或权威据为己有
senses.example: He assumed the right to speak for the whole group.
senses.exampleCN: 他擅自代表整个群体发言。
senses.why: This is the critical edge of assume: taking up something that was not offered. The word can describe both a legitimate takeover and an unwarranted seizure.
senses.whyCN: 这是 assume 的批判性边缘：拿起并未被给予的东西。这个词既能描述合法接管，也能描述不当夺取。

intro.en: Assume comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to take up'. Its senses spread from taking a thing onto oneself to taking a proposition into the mind, and finally to putting on an appearance.
intro.cn: assume 来自拉丁语“拿起来”的动词。它的义项从“把东西接到自己身上”扩展到“把命题拿进头脑”，最后到“戴上一副外表”。

items.en: First recorded as 'to arrogate, take upon oneself'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“僭取、把……据为己有”。

items.en: From Latin assumere/adsumere 'to take up, take to oneself, take besides, obtain in addition'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 assumere/adsumere“拿起、据为己有、另外拿、额外获得”。

items.en: assumere = ad- 'to, toward' + sumere 'to take', and sumere = sub- 'under' + emere 'to take, buy'.
items.cn: assumere = ad-“向”+ sumere“拿”，而 sumere = sub-“在下”+ emere“拿、买”。

items.en: emere goes back to PIE *em- 'to take, distribute'.
items.cn: emere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *em-“拿、分配”。

items.en: The sense 'to suppose, take for granted as the basis of argument' is recorded by the 1590s.
items.cn: “假定、作为论证基础而视为当然”的义项记录于 16 世纪 90 年代。

items.en: The sense 'to put on fictitiously' an appearance is recorded from around 1600.
items.cn: “假装具有某种外表”的义项记录于约 1600 年。

note.en: The first group shares the -sume root or looks close; the second contains other verbs of supposing and taking on.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -sume 词根或词形接近；第二组是其他表示“假定、承担”的动词。

entries.definition: to use up or eat. con- 'completely' + sumere 'take' gives 'take completely'.
entries.definitionCN: 消耗；吃光。con-“完全”+ sumere“拿”即“完全拿走”。

entries.definition: to begin again. re- 'again' + sumere 'take' gives 'take up again'.
entries.definitionCN: 重新开始。re-“再”+ sumere“拿”即“再次拿起”。

entries.definition: to assume with confidence, often too much. pre- 'before' + sumere 'take' gives 'take beforehand'.
entries.definitionCN: 假定，常含过度自信。pre-“先”+ sumere“拿”即“预先拿走”。

entries.definition: the word itself; note the silent -e in assuming and the noun assumption.
entries.definitionCN: 本词；注意 assuming 中不发音的 -e，以及名词 assumption。

entries.definition: to believe something without proof, often because it seems likely. It is stronger and more confident than assume.
entries.definitionCN: 无证据地相信某事，常因看起来很可能。它比 assume 更强、更自信。

entries.definition: to think something is probably true. It is more tentative and more conversational.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事可能为真。它更不确定，也更口语。

entries.definition: to accept a duty or role. It is the everyday phrase for assume in the responsibility sense.
entries.definitionCN: 接受职责或角色。它是 assume“承担责任”义的日常说法。

entries.definition: to pretend to have a feeling or condition. It is narrower and more literary than assume.
entries.definitionCN: 假装有某种感受或状况。它比 assume 更窄、更书面。

entries.definition: to take power or control suddenly and forcefully. It is much stronger than assume.
entries.definitionCN: 突然以武力夺取权力或控制。它比 assume 强得多。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- + sumere 'take', the -sumere family, and the literal theological sense 'taken up'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad- + sumere“拿”、-sumere 词族，以及字面神学义“被接上去”。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + sumere 'take' = 'take up'. Assume is literally lifting something and putting it on yourself.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ sumere“拿”=“拿起来”。assume 字面就是把某物拿起，放到自己身上。

normal.en: Consume, resume and presume share sumere 'take': take completely, take again, take beforehand.
normal.cn: consume、resume、presume 共享 sumere“拿”：完全拿走、再次拿起、预先拿走。

normal.en: An assumption is something taken up into the mind and held as true before proof arrives.
normal.cn: assumption 是被拿进头脑、在证据到来前就当作真的东西。

normal.en: Assume responsibility is the everyday phrase for lifting a duty onto your own shoulders.
normal.cn: assume responsibility 是把职责扛到自己肩上的日常说法。

normal.en: The Assumption in theology is literal: a person is taken up into heaven, from assumptus 'taken up'.
normal.cn: 神学中的 Assumption 是字面义：人被接升上天，来自 assumptus“被拿起”。

abstract.en: Abstractly, assume is a transfer onto the self: something outside — a duty, power, debt, quality, appearance or belief — is taken up and made one's own.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，assume 是一种“转移到自身”的操作：外部的东西——职责、权力、债务、性质、外表或信念——被拿起，变成自己的。

abstract.en: The transfer can be legitimate or not. Assume can mean both 'accept' and 'arrogate', depending on whether the thing was offered.
abstract.cn: 这种转移可以正当，也可以不正当。assume 既能表示“接受”，也能表示“僭取”，取决于该物是否被给予。

abstract.en: The mental branch is the same: a proposition is lifted from the world and placed at the base of thought as if true.
abstract.cn: 心智分支也是一样：一个命题被从世界中拿起，当作真的放在思维底部。

examples.en: I assume the meeting starts at nine unless I hear otherwise.
examples.cn: 我假定会议九点开始，除非另有通知。

examples.en: She assumed the role of manager after the director left.
examples.cn: 主任离开后，她承担了经理的角色。

examples.en: The situation assumed a more serious character overnight.
examples.cn: 一夜之间，局势呈现出更严重的性质。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿苏姆”——阿苏姆把别人的责任拿起来，放到自己肩上 → assume 承担、假定

root: 拉丁语 assumere“拿起、据为己有” = ad-“向”+ sumere“拿”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of assume, all built on one transfer: something outside the self is taken up and made one's own. It may be a belief, a duty, power, an appearance, a quality, a logical premise, a heavenly reception, a debt, or an unwarranted right.
sensesIntro.cn: assume 的九个义项都建立在一个转移上：自身之外的东西被拿起，变成自己的。它可以是信念、职责、权力、外表、性质、逻辑前提、升天、债务，或一项不正当的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifts something that was not on the body and places it on the self.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拿起原本不在身上的东西，把它放到自己身上。

branches.en: TAKING ON: a duty, power, debt or right is lifted onto the self, legitimately or not.
branches.cn: 承担：职责、权力、债务或权利被拿起放到自身，可能正当，也可能不正当。

branches.en: BELIEF: a proposition is taken into the mind and held as a premise.
branches.cn: 信念：命题被拿进头脑，作为前提持有。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: a mask or manner is put on like clothing.
branches.cn: 外表：面具或举止像衣服一样被穿上。

branches.en: QUALITY: a situation takes up a new form or character.
branches.cn: 性质：情况拿起一个新的形态或性质。

branches.en: THEOLOGY: a person is literally taken up into heaven.
branches.cn: 神学：人被字面意义上接升上天。

intro.en: Assume builds assumption, assumed, assuming, assumable and unassuming. The -tion, -ed and -ing forms carry the noun, adjective and participle.
intro.cn: assume 构成 assumption、assumed、assuming、assumable、unassuming。-tion、-ed、-ing 分别承担名词、形容词和分词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on sumere 'to take' (sub- + emere, PIE *em-): consume, resume and presume all describe different ways of taking.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 sumere“拿”（sub- + emere，原始印欧语 *em-）上：consume、resume、presume 都描述不同的“拿”的方式。

items.meaning: something taken as true; also the act of taking on a role
items.meaningCN: 假定；承担；就任（-ption 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The plan rests on a false assumption.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划建立在一个错误假定上。

items.meaning: taken as true, or taken on; also false or pretended
items.meaningCN: 假定的；承担的；冒称的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The assumed name was not his real one.
items.exampleCN: 这个 assumed name 不是他的真名。

items.meaning: the act of supposing; also 'if we assume that'
items.meaningCN: 假定；假设（-ing 构成分词、名词或连词）
items.example: Assuming the train is on time, we will arrive by noon.
items.exampleCN: 假设火车准点，我们中午前会到。

items.meaning: able to be taken on or supposed
items.meaningCN: 可承担的；可假定的（-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: The mortgage is assumable by the buyer.
items.exampleCN: 这笔抵押贷款可由买方承接。

items.meaning: not pretentious; modest
items.meaningCN: 不张扬的；谦逊的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: He is quiet and unassuming.
items.exampleCN: 他安静而谦逊。

items.meaning: based on assumption; presumptuous
items.meaningCN: 假定性的；僭越的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The argument is assumptive rather than evidential.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证是假定性的，而非基于证据。

items.meaning: to take on again
items.meaningCN: 重新承担；再次假定（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: The manager reassumed her duties after the leave.
items.exampleCN: 休假后经理重新承担了职责。

items.meaning: the legal act of accepting a known danger
items.meaningCN: 风险自担（法律短语）
items.example: The waiver records an assumption of risk.
items.exampleCN: 免责书记录了风险自担。

items.meaning: a false identity taken on by a person
items.meaningCN: 冒用的身份（assumed + identity 复合名词）
items.example: The spy travelled under an assumed identity.
items.exampleCN: 间谍以冒用身份旅行。

items.meaning: a formula for introducing a hypothesis
items.meaningCN: 让我们假定（固定短语）
items.example: Let us assume the data are correct.
items.exampleCN: 让我们假定数据是正确的。

latinEntries.meaning: to take completely, hence to use up
to take up again
to take beforehand, hence to suppose confidently
costly, taken up in expense
latinEntries.meaningCN: 奢华的（来自 sumere“拿”，引申为花费巨大）

definition_zh: 向……保证；使确信；确保；给……保险
definition_en: to promise confidently, make someone certain, or make something certain
core_image: 把一句“放心”稳稳放进对方心里
scene: 病床前，医生把手放在病人的肩上。 The doctor patted the patient's shoulder and assured her that the operation would be safe.
sceneCN: 这里 assure 是「使确信、安慰」（第 2 个义项：消除某人的疑虑）；句意：医生拍拍病人的肩，向她保证手术会很安全。

pos.zh: 向……保证；使确信；确保；给……保险

senses.title: Promise confidently to someone
senses.titleCN: 向某人保证：把话说定
senses.definition: to promise or state something confidently to someone
senses.definitionCN: 向某人自信地承诺或陈述某事
senses.example: I assure you that the work will be finished today.
senses.exampleCN: 我向你保证今天一定完成工作。
senses.why: The word is built on securus 'safe'. To assure is to give someone a secure word, a promise strong enough to remove doubt.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 securus“安全”上。assure 就是给某人一句稳妥的话，一句强到足以消除疑虑的承诺。

senses.title: Reassure and calm someone
senses.titleCN: 使安心：消除对方的担忧
senses.definition: to make someone feel less worried or more certain
senses.definitionCN: 使某人少担心或更确定
senses.example: The doctor assured her that the operation was routine.
senses.exampleCN: 医生让她放心，手术是常规操作。
senses.why: Fear is a lack of security. Assure addresses the worried person and puts certainty back in place.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧是安全感的缺失。assure 面向担忧的人，把确定性重新放回原处。

senses.title: Make an outcome certain
senses.titleCN: 确保：使结果成为确定
senses.definition: to make something certain to happen or be true
senses.definitionCN: 使某事确定会发生或为真
senses.example: Careful planning assured the success of the event.
senses.exampleCN: 周密计划确保了活动成功。
senses.why: Here the object is not a person but an outcome. Assure moves from giving confidence to making the thing itself secure.
senses.whyCN: 这里宾语不是人，而是结果。assure 从“给人信心”转向“让事情本身稳固”。

senses.title: Insure against loss
senses.titleCN: 给……保险：为风险提供保障
senses.definition: to insure a person's life or property against loss; British usage
senses.definitionCN: 为人的生命或财产提供损失保障；英式用法
senses.example: His life was assured for a large sum.
senses.exampleCN: 他的寿险保额很大。
senses.why: Assure and insure share the same Latin root. In British English, assure can still mean 'insure', especially for life assurance.
senses.whyCN: assure 与 insure 共享同一拉丁词根。在英式英语中，assure 仍可表示“给……保险”，尤用于 life assurance。

senses.title: State a fact with certainty
senses.titleCN: 确定地陈述：把事实说定
senses.definition: to state something as certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 把某事陈述为确定的事实
senses.example: He assured us that the door had been locked.
senses.exampleCN: 他向我们肯定地说门已经锁好了。
senses.why: A statement can be made secure by the speaker's confidence. Assure adds the force of certainty to the report.
senses.whyCN: 陈述可以因说话者的确信而变得稳固。assure 给报告加上确定性的力量。

senses.title: Make safe or secure
senses.titleCN: 使安全：保护起来
senses.definition: to make someone or something safe; archaic
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物安全；古旧用法
senses.example: The walls assured the town against attack.
senses.exampleCN: 城墙保护城镇免受攻击。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal layer: securus means 'free from care'. Assure once meant to make a person or place free from danger.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面层：securus 意为“无忧”。assure 曾表示使人或地方免于危险。

senses.title: Rest assured
senses.titleCN: 请放心：固定短语
senses.definition: in the phrase rest assured, meaning 'you may be certain'
senses.definitionCN: 用于 rest assured，表示“你可以放心”
senses.example: Rest assured that your application will be reviewed.
senses.exampleCN: 请放心，你的申请会被审核。
senses.why: The phrase tells the listener to remain in a secure state. Rest is the posture; assured is the condition of certainty.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语让听者保持在一个安全状态。rest 是姿势，assured 是确定的状态。

senses.title: Assure oneself
senses.titleCN: 使自己确信：主动核实
senses.definition: to make oneself certain about something
senses.definitionCN: 使自己确认某事
senses.example: She assured herself that the gas was off.
senses.exampleCN: 她确认了煤气已经关掉。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the act inward: the same person gives and receives the assurance.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把动作转向内部：同一个人既给出保证，也接受保证。

senses.title: Be assured of
senses.titleCN: 确信：对……有把握
senses.definition: in the phrase be assured of, meaning 'be certain about'
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be assured of，表示“对……有把握”
senses.example: You can be assured of our full support.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以确信我们会全力支持。
senses.why: The passive phrase describes a person held in certainty by someone else's promise. The security is received, not self-generated.
senses.whyCN: 这个被动短语描述一个人因他人的承诺而处于确定状态。安全感是被给予的，不是自己生成的。

intro.en: Assure and sure are doublets: both go back to Latin securus 'free from care', but they entered English by different routes. The core idea is making a person or outcome secure.
intro.cn: assure 与 sure 是同源异形词：两者都可追溯到拉丁语 securus“无忧”，但经不同路径进入英语。核心概念是让人或结果变得安全确定。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'reassure, give confidence to; make secure or safe, protect; bind by a pledge'.
items.cn: 最早记录意为“使安心、给予信心；使安全、保护；以誓约约束”。

items.en: From Old French asseurer 'to reassure, calm, protect, render sure' (12c.), Modern French assurer.
items.cn: 来自古法语 asseurer“使安心、安抚、保护、使确定”（12 世纪），现代法语 assurer。

items.en: From Vulgar Latin *assecurar, an assimilated form of ad- 'to' + securus 'safe, secure'.
items.cn: 来自俗拉丁语 *assecurar，是 ad-“向”+ securus“安全、稳固”的同化形式。

items.en: securus = se- 'free from' + cura 'care'. Literally 'without care', hence safe and untroubled.
items.cn: securus = se-“脱离”+ cura“忧虑”。字面“无忧”，因而安全、安定。

items.en: Sure is the same Latin word altered through Old French; secure entered directly from Latin. Assure, sure and secure form a doublet family.
items.cn: sure 是同一个拉丁词经古法语变形的结果；secure 直接从拉丁语进入。assure、sure、secure 构成同源异形词族。

items.en: Modern English keeps the promise and reassurance senses. Life assurance is the British insurance term; rest assured is a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 现代英语保留承诺与安慰义。life assurance 是英式保险术语；rest assured 是固定短语。

note.en: The first group is the classic assure/ensure/insure confusion; the second contains other verbs of promising and calming.
note.cn: 第一组是经典的 assure/ensure/insure 混淆组；第二组是其他表示“保证、安慰”的动词。

entries.definition: to make certain that something happens. It usually takes an event or result as its object, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 确保某事发生。它通常以事件或结果为宾语，而不是人。

entries.definition: to protect against loss by insurance. It is the financial and legal word.
entries.definitionCN: 通过保险防范损失。它是金融和法律用词。

entries.definition: to suppose or take on. It shares the ass- opening but not the 'secure' root.
entries.definitionCN: 假定；承担。它同样以 ass- 开头，但没有“安全”词根。

entries.definition: the word itself; compare its noun assurance and the adjective assured.
entries.definitionCN: 本词；比较名词 assurance 和形容词 assured。

entries.definition: to say that one will definitely do something. It is broader and does not always remove the other person's doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 说一定会做某事。它更宽，不总能消除对方的疑虑。

entries.definition: to promise that something will certainly happen, often with a formal or legal commitment.
entries.definitionCN: 保证某事一定发生，常带正式或法律承诺。

entries.definition: to make someone feel less worried. It focuses on the listener's emotion rather than the truth of the statement.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人少担心。它更关注听者的情绪，而不是陈述的真假。

entries.definition: to make someone believe that something is true. It stresses argument and evidence, not a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人相信某事为真。它强调论证和证据，而不是承诺。

entries.definition: to make something safe or fixed. It is the literal 'free from care' branch of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 使安全或固定。它是同一词根“无忧”的字面分支。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- + securus 'safe', the sure/secure doublet, and the fixed phrase rest assured.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad- + securus“安全”、sure/secure 同源词，以及固定短语 rest assured。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + securus 'safe' = 'make safe'. Assure is giving someone a secure word.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ securus“安全”=“使安全”。assure 是给某人一句稳妥的话。

normal.en: Sure and secure are doublets of the same Latin word; assure, sure and secure all carry the 'free from care' idea.
normal.cn: sure 与 secure 是同一个拉丁词的同源异形词；assure、sure、secure 都带“无忧”概念。

normal.en: Assurance is the noun: a promise, a feeling of certainty, or a life insurance policy.
normal.cn: assurance 是名词：承诺、确定感，或人寿保险。

normal.en: Rest assured is a fixed phrase: stay in a secure state, because the matter is certain.
normal.cn: rest assured 是固定短语：保持安心状态，因为事情已经确定。

normal.en: Assure someone of something is to put a guarantee into their hands, not just to say words.
normal.cn: assure someone of something 是把保证放进对方手里，而不只是说几句话。

abstract.en: Abstractly, assure is a transfer of certainty: one person has it, and gives enough of it to remove another person's doubt.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，assure 是确定性的转移：一个人拥有它，并给出足够的一份，消除另一个人的疑虑。

abstract.en: The certainty can be about a fact, a future outcome, a person's safety, or a financial risk.
abstract.cn: 这种确定性可以关于事实、未来结果、人身安全或财务风险。

abstract.en: So assure always has two directions: outward, calming a person; inward, making an outcome or the self secure.
abstract.cn: 所以 assure 总有两个方向：向外安抚他人；向内使结果或自身变得稳固。

examples.en: I assure you that no one will be dismissed.
examples.cn: 我向你保证不会有人被解雇。

examples.en: The nurse assured the patient that the test was painless.
examples.cn: 护士向病人保证这项检查不疼。

examples.en: Good preparation assured the team's success.
examples.cn: 充分的准备确保了团队的成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿秀”——阿秀拍着病人的肩说“放心”，把安全放回对方心里 → assure 使确信、保证

root: 古法语 asseurer，源自俗拉丁语 ad-“向”+ securus“安全”，核心是“使人或结果变得稳妥”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of assure, all built on one transfer of certainty: a secure word is given to a person, or security is made real for an outcome. The certainty may concern a promise, a worry, a result, insurance, a fact, safety, a fixed phrase, the self, or another's support.
sensesIntro.cn: assure 的九个义项都建立在一个确定性的转移上：把一句稳妥的话给人，或让某个结果真正稳固。这种确定性可以关于承诺、担忧、结果、保险、事实、安全、固定短语、自身或他人的支持。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a secure word is placed into a worried mind, or a lock is put on an uncertain outcome.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句稳妥的话被放进担忧的心里，或给不确定的结果加上一把锁。

branches.en: PROMISE: a confident statement is given to a person as a guarantee.
branches.cn: 承诺：一句自信的话作为保证给到某个人。

branches.en: REASSURE: the listener's fear is addressed and certainty is restored.
branches.cn: 安慰：回应听者的恐惧，把确定性重新放回原处。

branches.en: ENSURE: the object is an outcome, and the word makes it certain.
branches.cn: 确保：宾语是一个结果，这个词使它变得确定。

branches.en: INSURANCE AND SAFETY: life and property are protected; an older sense makes a place safe.
branches.cn: 保险与安全：生命和财产受到保护；较旧的义项使一个地方安全。

branches.en: FIXED PHRASES: rest assured, assure oneself and be assured of describe states of received certainty.
branches.cn: 固定短语：rest assured、assure oneself、be assured of 描述获得确定性的状态。

intro.en: Assure builds assurance, assured, assuredly, reassure and reassurance. The -ance and -ed forms carry the noun and the adjective; re- adds repetition or restoration.
intro.cn: assure 构成 assurance、assured、assuredly、reassure、reassurance。-ance 与 -ed 承担名词和形容词；re- 增加反复或恢复。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on cura 'care' and securus 'free from care': secure, sure, cure and curious all belong to this care-and-safety complex.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 cura“忧虑、照护”和 securus“无忧”上：secure、sure、cure、curious 都属于这个“照护与安全”词义群。

items.meaning: a promise; certainty; also life insurance
items.meaningCN: 保证；信心；人寿保险（-ance 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: She gave him her assurance of support.
items.exampleCN: 她向他保证会支持。

items.meaning: certain; confident; guaranteed
items.meaningCN: 确定的；有把握的；有保证的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: His assured manner calmed the room.
items.exampleCN: 他笃定的态度让全场安静下来。

items.meaning: certainly; without doubt
items.meaningCN: 确实地；肯定地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The plan will assuredly fail without funding.
items.exampleCN: 没有资金，这个计划肯定会失败。

items.meaning: the quality of being confident or certain
items.meaningCN: 确信；笃定（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: Her assuredness impressed the interviewers.
items.exampleCN: 她的笃定给面试官留下深刻印象。

items.meaning: to restore someone's confidence
items.meaningCN: 使安心；再保证（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: The teacher reassured the nervous student.
items.exampleCN: 老师安慰了紧张的学生。

items.meaning: the act or words that restore confidence
items.meaningCN: 安慰；再保证（re- + assure + -ance）
items.example: His reassurance helped her sleep.
items.exampleCN: 他的安慰帮她入睡。

items.meaning: giving confidence
items.meaningCN: 令人安心的；保证的（-ing 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: She spoke in an assuring tone.
items.exampleCN: 她用令人安心的语气说话。

items.meaning: not made certain; uncertain
items.meaningCN: 未获保证的；不确定的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: The unassured investors waited for news.
items.exampleCN: 未获保证的投资者等待消息。

items.meaning: confident in oneself
items.meaningCN: 自信的（self- + assure + -ed）
items.example: She became more self-assured after the course.
items.exampleCN: 课程之后她变得更自信。

items.meaning: a British term for life insurance
items.meaningCN: 人寿保险（英式说法，life + assurance 复合名词）
items.example: Life assurance protects the family financially.
items.exampleCN: 人寿保险为家庭提供经济保障。

latinEntries.meaning: safe; free from danger or care
latinEntries.meaningCN: 安全的；无忧的（se-“脱离”+ cura“忧虑”）

latinEntries.meaning: certain; confident
latinEntries.meaningCN: 确定的；确信的（securus 经古法语变形）

latinEntries.meaning: to heal or restore health; a remedy
latinEntries.meaningCN: 治愈；疗法（来自 cura“照护、忧虑”）

latinEntries.meaning: eager to know; literally 'full of care'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 好奇的（字面“充满关切”，来自 cura“忧虑”）

definition_en: to fasten or join something to something else, or to bind a person emotionally
core_image: 用钉子或夹子把两样东西固定在一起
scene: 电脑屏幕上是写好的邮件，回形针图标在附件栏旁。 She attached her resume to the email and clicked send.
sceneCN: 这里 attach 是「附上（文件）」（第 2 个义项：把文件附加到另一物）；句意：她把简历附到邮件里，然后点了发送。

senses.title: Fasten one thing to another
senses.titleCN: 系上：把两物固定在一起
senses.definition: to fasten or join one thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 把一物固定或连接到另一物上
senses.example: Attach the trailer to the back of the car.
senses.exampleCN: 把拖车系到车后。
senses.why: The oldest physical sense comes from a Germanic word for 'post, stake'. Something is pinned or fixed to a post, and attach means fastening.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理义来自日耳曼语“柱子、桩”。某物被钉或固定在桩上，attach 就表示系紧。

senses.title: Affix a document or label
senses.titleCN: 附上文件或标签：把一张纸加到另一物
senses.definition: to add a document, label, or note to something else
senses.definitionCN: 把文件、标签或便条加到另一物上
senses.example: Attach a copy of your passport to the form.
senses.exampleCN: 在表格上附一份护照复印件。
senses.why: A paper can be fixed to a file or form. The physical act of fastening becomes the bureaucratic act of adding a supporting document.
senses.whyCN: 纸可以固定在文件或表格上。物理上的系附变成行政上的“添加证明文件”。

senses.title: Connect equipment or a component
senses.titleCN: 连接设备或部件
senses.definition: to connect a device or part to a machine or system
senses.definitionCN: 把设备或部件连接到机器或系统
senses.example: Attach the monitor to the laptop with this cable.
senses.exampleCN: 用这根线把显示器连接到笔记本电脑。
senses.why: A component is joined to a larger system. Attach marks the connection point, whether the join is mechanical or electrical.
senses.whyCN: 部件被接到更大的系统上。attach 标出连接点，无论连接是机械的还是电气的。

senses.title: Attach importance or value
senses.titleCN: 重视：把重要性附到某事上
senses.definition: to give importance or significance to something
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某事重要性或意义
senses.example: The school attaches great importance to reading.
senses.exampleCN: 学校非常重视阅读。
senses.why: Importance is treated as a weight that can be attached to an object. What you attach importance to is what you tie value onto.
senses.whyCN: 重要性被看作可以附到对象上的重量。你 attach importance 的东西，就是你系上价值的东西。

senses.title: Be emotionally attached
senses.titleCN: 依恋：情感上系在某人或某物上
senses.definition: to feel affection for someone or something, so that separation is hard
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物产生感情，难以分离
senses.example: She is deeply attached to her old bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那辆旧自行车有很深的感情。
senses.why: Emotion is pictured as a bond. A person becomes attached when affection fastens them to the object, as a rope fastens one thing to another.
senses.whyCN: 情感被想象成一条纽带。当感情把人系到对象上，人就是 attached，像绳子把两物系在一起。

senses.title: Assign staff to a unit
senses.titleCN: 派驻：把人员临时编入某单位
senses.definition: to assign a person to a unit for a period, especially in the military or diplomacy
senses.definitionCN: 把某人临时编入某单位，尤用于军事或外交
senses.example: The officer was attached to the embassy for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这名军官被派驻大使馆一年。
senses.why: A person can be attached to a unit like a temporary part. The attachment is an administrative join, not a permanent transfer.
senses.whyCN: 人可以像临时部件一样被附到某个单位。这种 attachment 是行政上的连接，不是永久调动。

senses.title: Attach conditions to an agreement
senses.titleCN: 附加条件：把条款系到协议上
senses.definition: to add conditions or qualifications to an agreement or offer
senses.definitionCN: 给协议或提议增加条件或限制
senses.example: They attached several conditions to the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给贷款附加了几项条件。
senses.why: Conditions are tied onto an agreement. Attach conditions means the main thing does not stand alone; extra terms are fastened to it.
senses.whyCN: 条件被系到协议上。attach conditions 意味着主体并不单独成立，额外条款被附加上去。

senses.title: Seize property by law
senses.titleCN: 法律扣押：依法查封财产
senses.definition: to take legal possession of property by court order; legal
senses.definitionCN: 依法院命令取得财产的法律占有；法律用语
senses.example: The court attached his bank account.
senses.exampleCN: 法院查封了他的银行账户。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded English sense: to take or seize property by law. The legal attachment fastens a claim onto the property.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最早记录的义项：依法取得或扣押财产。法律上的 attachment 把一项请求权固定到财产上。

senses.title: Attach a file to a message
senses.titleCN: 附加文件：把文件随邮件发送
senses.definition: to add a file to an email or message
senses.definitionCN: 把文件添加到电子邮件或消息中
senses.example: Please attach the report to your reply.
senses.exampleCN: 请在回复中附上报告。
senses.why: Digital files are joined to messages as paper once was pinned to a letter. The metaphor keeps the physical image of fastening.
senses.whyCN: 数字文件被接到消息上，正如纸张曾被钉在信上。这个隐喻保留了“固定”的物理意象。

intro.en: Attach entered English as a legal word for seizing property, then became the everyday word for fastening. Its root is Germanic, not Latin: a stake or post to which something is fixed.
intro.cn: attach 以“依法扣押财产”的法律词进入英语，后来变成“系附”的日常词。它的词根是日耳曼语而非拉丁语：一根用来固定东西的桩。

items.en: First recorded in English as a legal term, 'to take or seize property or goods by law'.
items.cn: 最早记录为法律术语“依法取得或扣押财产或货物”。

items.en: From Old French atachier 'fasten; arrest' (11c.), earlier estachier 'to attach, fix; stake up, support'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 atachier“系紧；逮捕”（11 世纪），更早为 estachier“附着、固定；用桩支撑”。

items.en: The source is probably Frankish *stakjan or a similar Germanic word for a post or stake, from Proto-Germanic *stakon- 'a stake'.
items.cn: 来源可能是法兰克语 *stakjan 或类似的日耳曼语“柱子、桩”词，再往前是原始日耳曼语 *stakon-“桩”。

items.en: The Germanic stake word goes back to PIE *steg- 'pole, stick', the root also behind stake.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的“桩”可追溯到原始印欧语 *steg-“杆、棍”，stake 也出自这个词根。

items.en: The sense 'fasten, affix, connect', which is probably the original etymological sense, is recorded in English from around 1400.
items.cn: “系紧、附着、连接”这一大概更接近词源本义的义项，在英语中记录于约 1400 年。

items.en: The emotional sense 'join in affection' appears in the 1760s, giving attached 'fond, devoted' by 1793. Email attachments extend the physical image in the late 20th century.
items.cn: “情感上联结”的义项出现于 18 世纪 60 年代，1793 年产生 attached“依恋的”。电子邮件附件在 20 世纪晚期延伸了这一物理意象。

note.en: The first group is about spelling and the de-/at- contrast; the second is about other verbs of joining and binding.
note.cn: 第一组看拼写和 de-/at- 对比；第二组看其他表示“连接、系绑”的动词。

entries.definition: to unfasten or separate. de- 'apart' reverses attach.
entries.definitionCN: 拆卸；使分离。de-“分开”是 attach 的反向。

entries.definition: to try to hurt or defeat. It shares the at- opening but has a different root and meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 攻击；试图伤害或击败。它同样以 at- 开头，但词根和词义不同。

entries.definition: to reach or achieve. It comes from 'touch', not from 'stake'.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它来自“触摸”，不是“桩”。

entries.definition: a diplomatic official attached to an embassy. The accent and vowel differ from attach.
entries.definitionCN: 随员；使馆专员。重音和元音与 attach 不同。

entries.definition: to fix something firmly in place. It is the direct physical synonym of attach in its first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定。它是 attach 第一义的直接物理同义词。

entries.definition: to join two things so that they are linked. It is broader and often used for systems and ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 把两物连接起来。它更宽，常用于系统和想法。

entries.definition: to attach something, especially a label or stamp, in a formal or technical way.
entries.definitionCN: 附着某物，尤指标签或印章，较正式或技术化。

entries.definition: to tie or hold things together. It is stronger and often implies rope, rules, or obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 捆绑；约束。它更强，常暗示绳索、规则或义务。

entries.definition: to add something at the end, especially text or data. It is technical and sequential.
entries.definitionCN: 在末尾添加，尤指文本或数据。它较技术化，带顺序性。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Germanic 'stake' root, the de-/re- opposites, and the everyday email attachment.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：日耳曼语“桩”词根、de-/re- 反向前缀，以及日常电子邮件附件。

normal.en: The root is a stake or post: something is fixed to a post, and attach means fastening it there.
normal.cn: 词根是桩或柱子：某物被固定到桩上，attach 就是把它系在那里。

normal.en: Detach is the reverse: de- 'apart' + attach, to unfasten what was tied.
normal.cn: detach 是反向：de-“分开”+ attach，把系上的东西解开。

normal.en: Attachment is both a physical fastening and an emotional bond: a file attached to an email, a person attached to a friend.
normal.cn: attachment 既是物理固定，也是情感纽带：附在邮件上的文件，依恋朋友的人。

normal.en: Attach importance to something is to tie value onto it, as if importance were a weight you fasten.
normal.cn: attach importance to something 是把价值系到某事上，仿佛重要性是一块可以固定的重物。

normal.en: An email attachment keeps the old image: a file is pinned to the message, just as paper was pinned to a letter.
normal.cn: 电子邮件附件保留旧意象：文件被钉在消息上，正如纸张曾被钉在信上。

abstract.en: Abstractly, attach is a join with an anchor: one thing remains primary, and another is fixed to it.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，attach 是带锚点的连接：一物保持主体地位，另一物被固定到它上面。

abstract.en: The fixed thing can be physical (a trailer), informational (a file), institutional (an officer), emotional (a bond), or evaluative (importance).
abstract.cn: 被固定的东西可以是物理的（拖车）、信息的（文件）、制度的（军官）、情感的（纽带）或评价性的（重要性）。

abstract.en: So attach always implies asymmetry: there is a host and an addition, a main body and something fastened to it.
abstract.cn: 所以 attach 总暗示不对称：有一个主体和一个附加物，一个主件和一个系在它上面的东西。

examples.en: Attach the label to the outside of the box.
examples.cn: 把标签贴在箱子外面。

examples.en: Please attach your transcript to the application.
examples.cn: 请把成绩单附在申请材料中。

examples.en: The child is very attached to her grandmother.
examples.cn: 这个孩子非常依恋她的祖母。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿塔奇”——阿塔奇用夹子把简历夹到邮件上，一点发送 → attach 附上、连接

root: 古法语 atachier“系紧、固定”，可能源自法兰克语“桩、柱”，核心是“把一物固定到另一物上”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of attach, all built on one join: something is fastened to a host. The fastened thing may be a trailer, a document, a device, importance, an emotional bond, a person on assignment, a condition, a legal claim, or a file.
sensesIntro.cn: attach 的九个义项都建立在一个连接上：某物被固定到一个主体上。被固定之物可以是拖车、文件、设备、重要性、情感纽带、派驻人员、条件、法律请求权或文件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thing is pinned or tied to a post, so that it stays with the host.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被钉或系在一根桩上，因此与主体保持连接。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND DOCUMENTARY: a trailer, label, device or file is fastened to a host.
branches.cn: 物理与文件：拖车、标签、设备或文件被固定到一个主体上。

branches.en: VALUE: importance is treated as a weight tied onto an object.
branches.cn: 价值：重要性被当作系到对象上的一块重量。

branches.en: EMOTION: affection fastens a person to someone or something.
branches.cn: 情感：感情把人系到某人或某物上。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a person is temporarily attached to a unit.
branches.cn: 制度：一个人被临时编入某个单位。

branches.en: FORMAL: conditions are tied to an agreement; a legal claim is fastened to property.
branches.cn: 正式：条件被系到协议上；法律请求权被固定到财产上。

intro.en: Attach builds attachment, attached, attachable and unattached, and reverses with detach, detached and detachable. The -ment, -ed and -able suffixes are productive.
intro.cn: attach 构成 attachment、attached、attachable、unattached，并用 detach、detached、detachable 构成反向词族。-ment、-ed、-able 是能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: Attach has no reliable Latin cognate. Its root is Germanic, from a word for a post or stake, so the Latin list is left empty rather than filled with guesses.
latinIntro.cn: attach 没有可靠的拉丁同族词。它的词根是日耳曼语，来自“柱、桩”一词，因此拉丁词条留空，而不是用猜测填充。

items.meaning: a file added to a message; an emotional bond; the act of fastening
items.meaningCN: 附件；依恋；附着（-ment 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: Open the attachment to see the report.
items.exampleCN: 打开附件查看报告。

items.meaning: fastened; connected; fond of someone
items.meaningCN: 附加的；连接的；依恋的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: She is attached to her hometown.
items.exampleCN: 她依恋家乡。

items.meaning: able to be attached
items.meaningCN: 可附上的；可连接的（-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: The lens is attachable to any phone.
items.exampleCN: 这个镜头可以装在任何手机上。

items.meaning: not fastened; not emotionally committed
items.meaningCN: 未连接的；未订婚的；独立的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: He is still unattached and free to travel.
items.exampleCN: 他仍然单身，可以自由旅行。

items.meaning: to unfasten or separate
items.meaningCN: 拆卸；使分离（de- 表示“分开”）
items.example: Detach the cable before cleaning.
items.exampleCN: 清洁前先拔下电缆。

items.meaning: separated; emotionally distant
items.meaningCN: 分离的；超然的（de- + attach + -ed）
items.example: He spoke in a detached voice.
items.exampleCN: 他用超然的语气说话。

items.meaning: able to be detached
items.meaningCN: 可拆卸的（de- + attach + -able）
items.example: The hood has a detachable lining.
items.exampleCN: 这件外套有可拆内衬。

items.meaning: to attach again
items.meaningCN: 重新附上（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: Reattach the file after editing it.
items.exampleCN: 编辑后重新附上文件。

items.meaning: a file sent with an email
items.meaningCN: 电子邮件附件（email + attachment 复合名词）
items.example: The email attachment was too large to send.
items.exampleCN: 邮件附件太大，无法发送。

items.meaning: a place where something is fastened
items.meaningCN: 连接点；附着点（attachment + point 复合名词）
items.example: Check the attachment point on the harness.
items.exampleCN: 检查安全带上的连接点。

definition_en: to reach or achieve something, especially through effort
core_image: 伸手够到一个高处的目标，指尖终于碰到它
scene: 跑道上，运动员每天练习，计时器在终点等着。 She practised every day and finally attained a place on the Olympic team.
sceneCN: 这里 attain 是「实现、获得」（第 1 个义项：经过努力达到目标）；句意：她每天练习，最终获得了参加奥运会的资格。

senses.title: Achieve a goal through effort
senses.titleCN: 实现目标：努力之后达到
senses.definition: to succeed in reaching a goal, especially after effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力成功达到目标
senses.example: She attained her goal of running a marathon.
senses.exampleCN: 她实现了跑马拉松的目标。
senses.why: Latin attingere means 'to touch'. A goal is reached when effort finally touches it, as a hand touches a far object. Achievement is the last inch of that reach.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 attingere 意为“触摸”。当努力终于碰到目标，就像手碰到远处的物体，目标就达到了。成就是这段伸手的最后一段。

senses.title: Reach a level or standard
senses.titleCN: 达到水平：够到某个标准
senses.definition: to reach a particular level, standard, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 达到特定水平、标准或质量
senses.example: The country attained a high level of literacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家达到了很高的识字率。
senses.why: A level is imagined as a height. Attain means the level has been reached, and the thing now stands at that height.
senses.whyCN: 水平被想象成一个高度。attain 表示已经够到这个高度，事物现在站在那个位置上。

senses.title: Arrive at a place
senses.titleCN: 抵达：到达某地（书面）
senses.definition: to arrive at a place; literary
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地；书面语
senses.example: They attained the summit at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时抵达山顶。
senses.why: The oldest physical sense is simply reaching a place. The journey ends when the traveller touches the destination.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理义就是到达一个地方。旅程在旅人触及目的地时结束。

senses.title: Reach an age
senses.titleCN: 达到某年龄：活到或长到某个岁数
senses.definition: to reach a particular age
senses.definitionCN: 达到某个年龄
senses.example: The child attained the age of six last month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个孩子上个月满六岁。
senses.why: Age is a line on a scale. To attain an age is to reach that mark, a measured version of touching a point.
senses.whyCN: 年龄是刻度上的一条线。attain an age 就是到达那个刻度，是“触及某点”的度量版本。

senses.title: Gain a rank or office
senses.titleCN: 获得职位：达到某个身份
senses.definition: to gain a rank, position, or office
senses.definitionCN: 获得等级、职位或职务
senses.example: He attained the rank of captain after ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年后他获得了上尉军衔。
senses.why: Rank is social height. Attain marks the moment a person rises to that level and is entitled to its name.
senses.whyCN: 等级是社会高度。attain 标出一个人升到那个高度、有资格使用那个称号的时刻。

senses.title: Acquire knowledge or skill
senses.titleCN: 习得知识或技能：练到掌握
senses.definition: to gain knowledge or skill through learning
senses.definitionCN: 通过学习获得知识或技能
senses.example: She attained a high degree of fluency in French.
senses.exampleCN: 她的法语达到了很高的流利程度。
senses.why: Skill is a level that can be reached. Learning moves the learner upward until the skill is touched and held.
senses.whyCN: 技能是一个可以到达的水平。学习把学习者向上推，直到触及并掌握这项技能。

senses.title: Reach a physical maximum
senses.titleCN: 达到物理极限：升到最高点
senses.definition: to reach a maximum height, speed, or amount
senses.definitionCN: 达到最大高度、速度或数量
senses.example: The balloon attained a height of thirty kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 气球达到了三十公里的高度。
senses.why: A measured quantity has a top value. Attain describes the moment the quantity stops rising because the maximum has been touched.
senses.whyCN: 被测量的量有一个最高值。attain 描述该量停止上升、因为已触及最大值的时刻。

senses.title: Attain to something
senses.titleCN: 达到：正式搭配
senses.definition: in the formal phrase attain to, meaning 'reach or achieve'
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式短语 attain to，意为“达到、获得”
senses.example: The style attains to a kind of perfection.
senses.exampleCN: 这种风格达到了一种完美。
senses.why: The preposition to makes the movement explicit: the reaching is directed toward a standard. This formal pattern is close to the Latin source.
senses.whyCN: 介词 to 让运动方向显式化：伸手是朝一个标准去的。这个正式句式接近拉丁语来源。

intro.en: Attain began with the image of touching. Its Latin root is the verb 'to touch', and reaching a goal is pictured as coming into contact with it.
intro.cn: attain 从“触摸”的意象开始。它的拉丁词根是“触摸”动词，达到目标被想象成与目标接触。

items.en: First recorded as 'succeed in reaching, come so near as to touch'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“成功到达、近到可以触摸”。

items.en: From Old French ataindre 'to come up to, reach, attain, endeavor, strive' (11c.), Modern French atteindre.
items.cn: 来自古法语 ataindre“接近、到达、达到、努力、争取”（11 世纪），现代法语 atteindre。

items.en: From Vulgar Latin *attangere, corresponding to Latin attingere 'to touch; arrive at'.
items.cn: 来自俗拉丁语 *attangere，对应拉丁语 attingere“触摸；到达”。

items.en: attingere = ad- 'to' + tangere 'to touch'. The prefix directs the reaching; the root supplies contact.
items.cn: attingere = ad-“向”+ tangere“触摸”。前缀给出伸手方向，词根提供接触。

items.en: tangere goes back to PIE *tag- 'to touch, handle', the root behind contact, tactile and tangent.
items.cn: tangere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *tag-“触摸、操作”，contact、tactile、tangent 都出自这个词根。

items.en: Modern English keeps the abstract sense 'achieve' and a literary sense 'arrive at'. Attainment is the noun for an achievement or skill.
items.cn: 现代英语保留抽象义“获得、实现”和书面义“抵达”。名词 attainment 指成就或造诣。

note.en: The first group is about the -tain/-tempt spellings; the second contains other verbs of reaching and achieving.
note.cn: 第一组看 -tain/-tempt 拼写；第二组看其他表示“达到、实现”的动词。

entries.definition: to hold inside. con- 'together' + tenere 'hold', a different root from tangere.
entries.definitionCN: 包含；容纳。con-“一起”+ tenere“握持”，与 tangere 不同词根。

entries.definition: to get something. ob- 'toward' + tenere 'hold' gives 'get hold of'.
entries.definitionCN: 获得。ob-“向”+ tenere“握持”即“握住”。

entries.definition: to try. It comes from temptare 'try', not from tangere 'touch'.
entries.definitionCN: 尝试。它来自 temptare“试”，不是 tangere“触摸”。

entries.definition: the word itself; note the -ai- vowel and the formal phrase attain to.
entries.definitionCN: 本词；注意 -ai- 元音和正式短语 attain to。

entries.definition: to succeed in doing something after effort. It is the most common word for reaching a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力成功做成某事。它是“达到目标”最常用的词。

entries.definition: to arrive at a place, level, or amount. It is broader and more physical than attain.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地、水平或数量。它比 attain 更宽，也更物理。

entries.definition: to complete a task or purpose. It stresses finishing rather than reaching a level.
entries.definitionCN: 完成一项任务或目的。它强调完成，而不是达到某个水平。

entries.definition: to obtain something, especially gradually. It stresses the increase or acquisition.
entries.definitionCN: 获得，尤指逐渐获得。它强调增加或获取。

entries.definition: to obtain something with effort, especially something valuable. It is more formal than get.
entries.definitionCN: 努力获得，尤指有价值之物。它比 get 正式。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- + tangere 'touch', the *tag- touch family, and the formal phrase attain to.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad- + tangere“触摸”、*tag- 触摸词族，以及正式短语 attain to。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + tangere 'touch' = 'touch toward'. Attain is reaching until your hand touches the goal.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ tangere“触摸”=“朝……触摸”。attain 就是伸手直到碰到目标。

normal.en: Contact, tactile and tangent share the *tag- 'touch' root with attain: all involve contact.
normal.cn: contact、tactile、tangent 与 attain 共享 *tag-“触摸”词根：都涉及接触。

normal.en: Attain a level is to touch a height; attain an age is to touch a mark on a scale.
normal.cn: attain a level 是碰到一个高度；attain an age 是碰到刻度上的一个点。

normal.en: Attainment is the noun: the achievement itself, or the level of skill reached.
normal.cn: attainment 是名词：成就本身，或达到的技能水平。

normal.en: Attain to is the formal pattern: the reaching is directed toward a high standard.
normal.cn: attain to 是正式句式：伸手是朝一个高标准去的。

abstract.en: Abstractly, attain is effort ending in contact: a reach that finally touches its object.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，attain 是以接触告终的努力：一次终于碰到对象的伸手。

abstract.en: The object can be a place, a level, an age, a rank, a skill, a maximum, or a standard.
abstract.cn: 对象可以是地点、水平、年龄、职位、技能、极限或标准。

abstract.en: So attain always implies both motion and a threshold. It is not mere possession; it is arrival at something previously out of reach.
abstract.cn: 所以 attain 总含运动与门槛两层：不只是拥有，而是抵达此前够不到的东西。

examples.en: She attained a high level of proficiency in English.
examples.cn: 她的英语达到了很高的熟练程度。

examples.en: The company attained its sales target last quarter.
examples.cn: 公司上季度达到了销售目标。

examples.en: These goals are difficult but attainable.
examples.cn: 这些目标很难，但可以实现。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿泰恩”——阿泰恩每天练习，终于伸手够到奥运资格 → attain 达到、获得

root: 古法语 ataindre，源自拉丁语 attingere“触摸、到达” = ad-“向”+ tangere“触摸”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of attain, all built on one reach: effort moves toward a threshold and finally touches it. The threshold may be a goal, a level, a place, an age, a rank, a skill, a maximum, or a formal standard.
sensesIntro.cn: attain 的八个义项都建立在一个伸手上：努力朝一个门槛移动，最终碰到它。这个门槛可以是目标、水平、地点、年龄、职位、技能、极限或正式标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches toward a high object and the fingertips touch it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向高处的东西，指尖终于碰到它。

branches.en: GOAL: effort reaches a desired end, or formally attains to a standard.
branches.cn: 目标：努力到达期望的终点，或正式达到某个标准。

branches.en: LEVEL AND MAXIMUM: a measured height or top value is touched.
branches.cn: 水平与极限：一个被度量的高度或最高值被触及。

branches.en: PLACE: a traveller arrives at a destination.
branches.cn: 地点：旅人抵达目的地。

branches.en: MARK AND RANK: an age is reached; a social rank is gained.
branches.cn: 刻度与等级：达到某个年龄；获得某个社会等级。

branches.en: SKILL: learning brings a person to a level of knowledge or ability.
branches.cn: 技能：学习把人带到某个知识或能力水平。

intro.en: Attain builds attainment, attainable and unattainable. The -ment and -able suffixes carry the result noun and the possibility adjective.
intro.cn: attain 构成 attainment、attainable、unattainable。-ment 与 -able 分别承担结果名词和可能性形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on tangere 'to touch' (PIE *tag-): contact, tactile and tangent all describe touching or meeting a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 tangere“触摸”（原始印欧语 *tag-）上：contact、tactile、tangent 都描述接触或碰到表面。

items.meaning: the achievement of a goal, or a level of skill
items.meaningCN: 达到；成就；造诣（-ment 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: Educational attainment varies across the region.
items.exampleCN: 该地区的教育程度参差不齐。

items.meaning: able to be reached or achieved
items.meaningCN: 可达到的；可实现的（-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: The target is ambitious but attainable.
items.exampleCN: 这个目标雄心勃勃，但可以实现。

items.meaning: impossible to reach or achieve
items.meaningCN: 无法达到的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: Perfect fluency is an unattainable ideal.
items.exampleCN: 完美流利是无法达到的理想。

items.meaning: the quality of being attainable
items.meaningCN: 可达性；可实现性（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: Engineers questioned the attainability of the speed.
items.exampleCN: 工程师质疑这个速度是否可达。

items.meaning: reached or achieved
items.meaningCN: 已达到的；获得的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The attained level was higher than expected.
items.exampleCN: 达到的水平高于预期。

items.meaning: the process of reaching a goal
items.meaningCN: 达到；获得（-ing 构成分词或动名词）
items.example: Attaining fluency takes years of practice.
items.exampleCN: 达到流利需要多年练习。

items.meaning: the loss of civil rights after a death sentence; a historical legal term
items.meaningCN: 褫夺公权（历史法律术语，与 attain 有词源关联）
items.example: The old law of attainder was abolished.
items.exampleCN: 旧的褫夺公权法已被废除。

items.meaning: a formal phrase meaning 'reach or achieve'
items.meaningCN: 达到（正式短语 attain to）
items.example: The painting attains to greatness.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画达到了伟大的境界。

items.meaning: the highest level of education a person has completed
items.meaningCN: 教育程度（educational + attainment 复合名词）
items.example: Educational attainment is linked to income.
items.exampleCN: 教育程度与收入相关。

items.meaning: an achievement gained through great effort
items.meaningCN: 来之不易的成就（hard-won + attainment 复合名词）
items.example: The award recognised a hard-won attainment.
items.exampleCN: 这个奖项认可了一项来之不易的成就。

latinEntries.meaning: a touching or meeting; communication
latinEntries.meaningCN: 接触；联系（con-“一起”+ tangere“触摸”）

latinEntries.meaning: relating to the sense of touch
a line that touches a curve at one point
not touched; undamaged
latinEntries.meaningCN: 完整的；未受损的（in-“不”+ tangere“触摸”）

definition_zh: 尝试；试图；企图；（n.）努力；未遂
definition_en: to try to do something, or a try or effort
core_image: 向一个难关伸手，不一定够得到
scene: 攀岩者站在岩壁下，绳子和保护点都已系好。 The climber attempted the hard route for the first time and slipped halfway up.
sceneCN: 这里 attempt 是「尝试」（第 1 个义项：试图完成困难的事）；句意：攀岩者第一次尝试这条高难度路线，爬到一半滑了下来。

senses.title: Try to do something
senses.titleCN: 尝试：动手去做一件难事
senses.definition: to try to do something, especially something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 试图做某事，尤指困难的事
senses.example: He attempted to fix the engine himself.
senses.exampleCN: 他试图自己修好发动机。
senses.why: Latin attemptare is 'to try, make trial of'. The word starts with an effort directed at a task, before success or failure is known.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 attemptare 是“尝试、试行”。这个词从指向任务的一次努力开始，此时成败尚未可知。

senses.title: A try or effort
senses.titleCN: 尝试：一次努力的名词形式
senses.definition: an act of trying to do something
senses.definitionCN: 尝试做某事的动作
senses.example: Her first attempt at baking bread failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一次尝试烤面包失败了。
senses.why: The noun turns the effort into a countable event. An attempt has a beginning, an effort, and an outcome, successful or not.
senses.whyCN: 名词把努力变成可计数的事件。一次 attempt 有开始、有努力、有结果，无论成败。

senses.title: Try a difficult feat
senses.titleCN: 挑战：尝试完成高难动作
senses.definition: to try to achieve a difficult feat, such as a record or a climb
senses.definitionCN: 试图完成高难壮举，如纪录或攀登
senses.example: The climber attempted the north face in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 攀岩者在冬天尝试北壁。
senses.why: A feat is a height that may be out of reach. Attempt marks the reach without promising that the fingers will touch.
senses.whyCN: 壮举是一个可能够不到的高度。attempt 标出这次伸手，却并不保证指尖能碰到。

senses.title: Attempt a crime
senses.titleCN: 犯罪未遂：试图实施犯罪
senses.definition: to try to commit a crime without completing it; legal
senses.definitionCN: 试图实施犯罪但未完成；法律用语
senses.example: He was charged with attempted robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控抢劫未遂。
senses.why: Law separates the intention and the act. An attempted crime is an effort that came close but did not reach completion.
senses.whyCN: 法律把意图和行为分开。attempted crime 是一次已接近但未完成的努力。

senses.title: Attempt someone's life
senses.titleCN: 企图杀害：正式说法
senses.definition: to try to kill someone; formal or legal
senses.definitionCN: 试图杀害某人；正式或法律说法
senses.example: Someone attempted the minister's life last night.
senses.exampleCN: 昨晚有人企图刺杀部长。
senses.why: The object is a life, and the attempt is a violent reach toward ending it. This is the 'attack' branch recorded in the 1580s.
senses.whyCN: 宾语是生命，attempt 是朝终结它而去的一次暴力伸手。这是 16 世纪 80 年代记录的“攻击”分支。

senses.title: Try to answer or solve
senses.titleCN: 尝试解答：向问题伸手
senses.definition: to try to answer a question or solve a problem
senses.definitionCN: 试图回答问题或解决问题
senses.example: Students may attempt only three questions.
senses.exampleCN: 学生只能尝试回答三个问题。
senses.why: A question is a task with an unknown answer. Attempt is the effort to reach it, whether or not the answer is found.
senses.whyCN: 问题是一个答案未知的任务。attempt 是够向它的努力，无论最终是否找到答案。

senses.title: Attempt the impossible
senses.titleCN: 挑战不可能：固定说法
senses.definition: to try something widely believed to be impossible
senses.definitionCN: 尝试众人认为不可能的事
senses.example: They attempted the impossible and nearly succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挑战不可能，几乎成功了。
senses.why: The phrase pushes the image to its limit: the reach is made even when the object is known to be beyond reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把意象推到极限：即使知道对象够不到，仍然伸手。

senses.title: In an attempt to
senses.titleCN: 为了尝试：目的短语
senses.definition: in the phrase in an attempt to, meaning 'in order to try to'
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in an attempt to，表示“为了尝试……”
senses.example: He called in an attempt to explain.
senses.exampleCN: 他打电话来，试图解释。
senses.why: The phrase names the purpose of an action. The action is performed as part of an effort whose success is not yet known.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语说明一个行动的目的。行动作为一次努力的一部分发生，其成败尚未可知。

intro.en: Attempt comes from a Latin verb for trying or testing. The noun follows the verb, and the violent 'attack' sense appears later.
intro.cn: attempt 来自拉丁语“尝试、试探”的动词。名词跟随动词出现，暴力的“攻击”义后来才产生。

items.en: First recorded as a verb, 'seek or try to do, make an effort to perform'.
items.cn: 最早记录为动词“寻求或试图做、努力完成”。

items.en: From Old French atempter (14c.), earlier atenter 'to try, attempt, test', Modern French attenter.
items.cn: 来自古法语 atempter（14 世纪），更早为 atenter“尝试、试图、测试”，现代法语 attenter。

items.en: From Latin attemptare 'to try, make trial of; tamper with; attack, assail'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 attemptare“尝试、试行；干预；攻击、袭击”。

items.en: attemptare = ad- 'to, toward' + temptare 'to try, test, feel out'.
items.cn: attemptare = ad-“向”+ temptare“尝试、测试、试探”。

items.en: The noun attempt, 'a putting forth of effort in a difficult or uncertain endeavor', is recorded from the 1530s.
items.cn: 名词 attempt“在困难或不确定的事业中付出努力”记录于 16 世纪 30 年代。

items.en: The sense 'effort to accomplish something by violence', especially an assault on someone's life, appears in the 1580s.
items.cn: “以暴力完成某事”的义项，尤指袭击他人生命，出现于 16 世纪 80 年代。

note.en: The first group is about the tempt/attempt spelling; the second contains other words for trying.
note.cn: 第一组看 tempt/attempt 拼写；第二组看其他表示“尝试”的词。

entries.definition: to lure or entice someone. It comes from the same temptare 'test' root but has a different prefix history.
entries.definitionCN: 引诱；诱惑。它来自同一个 temptare“试探”词根，但前缀历史不同。

entries.definition: to reach or achieve. It comes from 'touch', not from 'try'.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它来自“触摸”，不是“尝试”。

entries.definition: to be present at or pay attention to. It comes from 'stretch toward'.
entries.definitionCN: 出席；注意。它来自“朝……伸展”。

entries.definition: the word itself; note the noun and verb share the same form except for the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 本词；注意名词和动词形式相同，只有复数加 -s。

entries.definition: to make an effort to do something. It is the most everyday and least formal word.
entries.definitionCN: 努力做某事。它是最日常、最不正式的词。

entries.definition: to try hard over time. It is formal and often used for serious or sustained effort.
entries.definitionCN: 长期努力尝试。它较正式，常用于严肃或持续的努力。

entries.definition: an attempt or the energy used in trying. It is the noun for the work, not the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 尝试，或尝试所用的精力。它是“努力”的名词，而不是动作本身。

entries.definition: an attempt to achieve something, especially in a competition or auction.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成某事的尝试，尤用于竞争或拍卖。

entries.definition: to try something risky or new. It stresses the risk more than attempt.
entries.definitionCN: 冒险尝试新事物。它比 attempt 更强调风险。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- + temptare 'try', the tempt family, and the legal phrase attempted crime.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad- + temptare“尝试”、tempt 词族，以及法律短语 attempted crime。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + temptare 'try' = 'try toward'. Attempt is an effort directed at a task.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ temptare“尝试”=“朝……尝试”。attempt 是指向任务的努力。

normal.en: Tempt and attempt share temptare 'test': to tempt someone is to test their resistance; to attempt is to test your own ability.
normal.cn: tempt 与 attempt 共享 temptare“试探”：诱惑是试探对方的抵抗力；尝试是试探自己的能力。

normal.en: An attempt has three parts: the intention, the effort, and the outcome. The word covers all three except the final result.
normal.cn: 一次 attempt 有三部分：意图、努力、结果。这个词覆盖前三者，只不保证最后的结果。

normal.en: Attempted murder is a legal phrase: the intention and effort are present, but completion is not.
normal.cn: attempted murder 是法律短语：意图和努力都在，但完成不在。

normal.en: In an attempt to explains purpose: the action is part of an effort whose outcome is still open.
normal.cn: in an attempt to 说明目的：该行动是一次努力的一部分，结果仍未定。

abstract.en: Abstractly, attempt is a reach without a guarantee. It is defined by effort, not by success.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，attempt 是一次没有保证的伸手。它由努力定义，而不由成功定义。

abstract.en: The object can be a task, a record, a crime, a life, a question, or something impossible.
abstract.cn: 对象可以是任务、纪录、犯罪、生命、问题或不可能之事。

abstract.en: So attempt always leaves a gap between trying and achieving. That gap is what the noun measures.
abstract.cn: 所以 attempt 总在“试”与“成”之间留下一个缺口。名词测量的正是这个缺口。

examples.en: She attempted to climb the wall without a rope.
examples.cn: 她试图不用绳子攀上那面墙。

examples.en: The rescue was a brave attempt but failed.
examples.cn: 那次救援是一次勇敢的尝试，但失败了。

examples.en: He was found guilty of attempted theft.
examples.cn: 他被判盗窃未遂。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿坦普特”——阿坦普特伸手去抓岩点，没抓到却挂在了绳上 → attempt 尝试、试图

root: 拉丁语 attemptare = ad-“向”+ temptare“尝试、试探”，核心是“朝目标伸手试一试”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of attempt, all built on one reach: effort goes toward something without a guarantee of touching it. The target may be a task, an effort itself, a difficult feat, a crime, a life, a question, the impossible, or a stated purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: attempt 的八个义项都建立在一个伸手上：努力朝某物而去，却不保证碰到它。目标可以是任务、努力本身、高难壮举、犯罪、生命、问题、不可能之事或一个说明的目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches toward a hard object; it may or may not touch it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向一个难够的东西，碰不碰得到并不确定。

branches.en: TASK: an effort is directed at a job or a question.
branches.cn: 任务：努力指向一项工作或一个问题。

branches.en: EFFORT NOUN: the try becomes a countable event, or a stated purpose.
branches.cn: 努力名词：尝试变成可计数的事件，或说明目的。

branches.en: FEAT: a record, a climb or the impossible is attempted.
branches.cn: 壮举：尝试纪录、攀登或不可能之事。

branches.en: CRIME: the law separates the attempt from the completed act.
branches.cn: 犯罪：法律把未遂与完成的行为分开。

branches.en: ATTACK: a violent reach toward someone's life.
branches.cn: 攻击：朝他人生命而去的一次暴力伸手。

intro.en: Attempt builds attempted, attempting, attemptable and reattempt. The -ed and -able forms are the productive parts, and the noun takes -s in the plural.
intro.cn: attempt 构成 attempted、attempting、attemptable、reattempt。-ed 与 -able 是能产部分，名词复数加 -s。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on temptare 'to try, test': temptation and tentative both come from the same testing root.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 temptare“尝试、试探”上：temptation 与 tentative 都来自同一个“试探”词根。

items.meaning: tried but not completed, especially of a crime
items.meaningCN: 未遂的；尝试过的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: He was charged with attempted robbery.
items.exampleCN: 他被控抢劫未遂。

items.meaning: in the process of trying
items.meaningCN: 正在尝试的（-ing 构成分词或动名词）
items.example: The team is attempting a new route.
items.exampleCN: 团队正在尝试一条新路线。

items.meaning: more than one try, or he/she tries
items.meaningCN: 多次尝试；他/她尝试（-s 构成复数或三单）
items.example: Her attempts to learn the piano paid off.
items.exampleCN: 她学钢琴的多次尝试有了回报。

items.meaning: able to be tried
items.meaningCN: 可尝试的（-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: The climb is difficult but attemptable.
items.exampleCN: 这条攀登路线很难，但可以尝试。

items.meaning: not tried
items.meaningCN: 未尝试的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: The final question was left unattempted.
items.exampleCN: 最后一道题没有尝试作答。

items.meaning: to try again
items.meaningCN: 再次尝试（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: He reattempted the exam in June.
items.exampleCN: 他六月再次尝试考试。

items.meaning: the crime of trying to kill someone
items.meaningCN: 谋杀未遂（attempted + murder 复合名词）
items.example: Attempted murder carries a serious sentence.
items.exampleCN: 谋杀未遂会判重刑。

items.meaning: an act of trying to kill someone
items.meaningCN: 企图杀害某人（固定短语）
items.example: There was an attempt on the president's life.
items.exampleCN: 有人企图刺杀总统。

items.meaning: a try that did not succeed
items.meaningCN: 失败的尝试（failed + attempt 复合名词）
items.example: The failed attempt taught them a lot.
items.exampleCN: 这次失败让他们学到很多。

items.meaning: the earliest try
items.meaningCN: 第一次尝试（first + attempt 复合名词）
items.example: She succeeded on her first attempt.
items.exampleCN: 她第一次尝试就成功了。

latinEntries.meaning: to test or entice someone
latinEntries.meaningCN: 诱惑；试探（来自 temptare“尝试、试探”）

latinEntries.meaning: the act of tempting or the desire to yield
done as a trial; not final
latinEntries.meaningCN: 试探性的；暂定的（来自 tentare“尝试”+ -ive）

latinEntries.meaning: a try or effort

definition_zh: 把……归因于；把……归于；属性；定语
definition_en: to say that something is caused by or belongs to someone, or a quality that belongs to something
core_image: 把一张写着“属于他”的标签，贴到原因或性质上
scene: 球场上，记者把麦克风伸向守门员。 The reporter attributed the team's victory to the goalkeeper's several key saves.
sceneCN: 这里 attribute 是「归功于」（第 2 个义项：把成功归给某人）；句意：记者把球队的胜利归功于守门员的几次关键扑救。

pos.zh: 把……归因于；把……归于；认为……属于（动词重音在后）
属性；特征；定语（名词重音在前）

collocations.zh: 把 A 归因于 B

senses.title: Explain a cause by assigning it
senses.titleCN: 归因：把结果的原因贴到某处
senses.definition: to say that something is caused by a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 说某事由某个特定因素引起
senses.example: They attribute the delay to bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把延误归因于恶劣天气。
senses.why: Latin attribuere is 'to give to'. A cause is given to a factor: the effect is explained by assigning it a source.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 attribuere 是“给”。原因被给到一个因素：通过给结果指定来源来解释它。

senses.title: Credit an achievement to someone
senses.titleCN: 归功于：把成功贴到某人身上
senses.definition: to say that someone or something deserves credit for a success
senses.definitionCN: 说某人或某物应对成功受功
senses.example: She attributes her success to hard work and luck.
senses.exampleCN: 她把成功归功于努力和运气。
senses.why: Credit is a value assigned to a person. Attribute gives the achievement back to the one believed to have produced it.
senses.whyCN: 功劳是被分配给某个人的价值。attribute 把成就还给被认为产生它的人。

senses.title: Regard something as a characteristic
senses.titleCN: 视为特征：把性质贴到对象上
senses.definition: to regard a quality as belonging to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 把某种性质看作属于某人或某物
senses.example: We attribute intelligence to many animals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们认为许多动物具有智力。
senses.why: A quality is treated as a possession. To attribute intelligence to an animal is to say intelligence belongs to it.
senses.whyCN: 性质被当作一种所有物。把智力归给动物，就是说智力属于它。

senses.title: A quality or feature
senses.titleCN: 属性：属于某物的一种性质
senses.definition: a quality or feature belonging to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人或某物的性质或特征
senses.example: Patience is an essential attribute of a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是教师必备的品质。
senses.why: The noun is the thing given in the verb sense. What can be attributed to a subject is an attribute of that subject.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是动词义中被给出的东西。能被归给一个主体的，就是该主体的 attribute。

senses.title: A grammatical modifier
senses.titleCN: 定语：修饰名词的成分
senses.definition: a word or phrase that modifies a noun; grammar
senses.definitionCN: 修饰名词的词或短语；语法术语
senses.example: In 'red car', red is an attributive adjective.
senses.exampleCN: 在 red car 中，red 是定语形容词。
senses.why: Grammar attaches a quality to a noun. The modifier is an attribute because it is 'given to' the noun as a property.
senses.whyCN: 语法把一种性质附到名词上。修饰语是 attribute，因为它作为属性被“给到”名词。

senses.title: A logical property
senses.titleCN: 逻辑属性：主词具有的性质
senses.definition: a property that can be predicated of a subject; logic
senses.definitionCN: 可以谓述一个主词的性质；逻辑术语
senses.example: Being mortal is an attribute of humans.
senses.exampleCN: 会死是人的一个属性。
senses.why: Logic formalises the same structure: a subject has properties. Attribute names whatever can be said to belong to the subject.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑形式化了同样的结构：主词拥有性质。attribute 指任何可以被称为属于主词的东西。

senses.title: A computing metadata field
senses.titleCN: 计算机属性：描述对象的数据字段
senses.definition: a field or property that describes an object in computing
senses.definitionCN: 描述计算机对象的数据字段
senses.example: Each file has a read-only attribute.
senses.exampleCN: 每个文件都有一个只读属性。
senses.why: A digital object is described by attached properties. Attribute is the technical name for a named piece of data belonging to that object.
senses.whyCN: 数字对象由附着的性质来描述。attribute 是属于该对象的具名数据的技术名称。

senses.title: Assign authorship or ownership
senses.titleCN: 认定作者或归属：把作品贴给某人
senses.definition: to believe that a work was made by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认为某作品由某人创作
senses.example: The painting is attributed to Leonardo.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画被认定出自达·芬奇。
senses.why: Authorship is a property given to a person. Attribution is the scholarly act of deciding whose mark a work carries.
senses.whyCN: 作者身份是被给到某人的属性。attribution 是学术上判定作品带有谁印记的行为。

senses.title: Assign blame or responsibility
senses.titleCN: 归咎：把责任贴到某人身上
senses.definition: to say that someone is responsible for a fault
senses.definitionCN: 说某人应对过错负责
senses.example: The report attributes the accident to human error.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把事故归咎于人为失误。
senses.why: Blame is a negative value assigned to a cause. Attribute can give fault to a person, just as it gives credit.
senses.whyCN: 责任是被分配给原因的一种负价值。attribute 可以把过错给人，正如它可以把功劳给人。

intro.en: Attribute comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to give to'. A quality or cause is given to a subject, and the noun names whatever has been given.
intro.cn: attribute 来自拉丁语“给”的动词。性质或原因被给到一个主体，名词则指被给出的东西。

items.en: First recorded as a verb, 'to assign as a quality or cause'.
items.cn: 最早记录为动词“作为性质或原因归于”。

items.en: From Latin attribuere 'to assign, allot, associate, bestow; ascribe, impute'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 attribuere“分配、划给、关联、授予；归因、归咎”。

items.en: attribuere = ad- 'to' + tribuere 'to assign, allot, grant, bestow, pay'.
items.cn: attribuere = ad-“向”+ tribuere“分配、划给、授予、支付”。

items.en: tribuere comes from tribus 'a division, tribe', originally the division of the Roman people into tribes.
items.cn: tribuere 来自 tribus“划分、部落”，原指罗马人民被划分成的部落。

items.en: The noun attribute, 'a quality ascribed to a person or thing', is recorded from the 1580s.
items.cn: 名词 attribute“被归于某人或某物的性质”记录于 16 世纪 80 年代。

items.en: The grammatical sense 'modifier of a noun' is recorded from 1751. The computing sense develops in the 20th century.
items.cn: 语法义“名词的修饰语”记录于 1751 年。计算机义在 20 世纪发展出来。

note.en: The first group shares the tribuere root or looks close; the second contains other words for ascribing and for qualities.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tribuere 词根或词形接近；第二组是其他表示“归因”和“性质”的词。

entries.definition: to give something to a common fund or effort. con- 'together' + tribuere 'give' gives 'give together'.
entries.definitionCN: 贡献；捐助。con-“一起”+ tribuere“给”即“一起给”。

entries.definition: to give out among many. dis- 'apart' + tribuere 'give' gives 'give apart'.
entries.definitionCN: 分配；分发。dis-“分开”+ tribuere“给”即“分开给”。

entries.definition: a payment or expression of respect given to someone. It is the noun from the same giving root.
entries.definitionCN: 贡品；致敬。它是同一“给予”词根的名词。

entries.definition: the word itself; the verb stresses the second syllable, the noun the first.
entries.definitionCN: 本词；动词重音在第二音节，名词重音在第一音节。

entries.definition: to say that something is caused by or belongs to someone. It is very close to attribute but more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 说某事由某人引起或属于某人。它与 attribute 很近，但更正式。

entries.definition: to say that someone deserves praise for something. It is the positive side of attribute.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某人应因某事受赞扬。它是 attribute 的正面一面。

entries.definition: to give a task, role, or cause to someone. It overlaps with attribute in the cause sense.
entries.definitionCN: 把任务、角色或原因给某人。它在“原因”义上与 attribute 重叠。

entries.definition: a quality or characteristic of something. It is the general noun for what an attribute is.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的性质或特征。它是 attribute 所指之物的一般名词。

entries.definition: a characteristic of a person or thing. It is broader and often evaluative.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物的特征。它更宽，常带评价性。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ad- + tribuere 'give', the tribute/contribute family, and the grammatical term attributive.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ad- + tribuere“给”、tribute/contribute 词族，以及语法术语 attributive。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + tribuere 'give' = 'give to'. An attribute is something given to a subject as belonging to it.
normal.cn: ad-“向”+ tribuere“给”=“给到”。attribute 就是被给到主体、属于它的东西。

normal.en: Contribute, distribute and tribute share tribuere 'give': give together, give apart, give as tribute.
normal.cn: contribute、distribute、tribute 共享 tribuere“给”：一起给、分开给、作为贡品给。

normal.en: The verb and noun differ in stress: attribute /əˈtrɪbjuːt/ vs attribute /ˈætrɪbjuːt/.
normal.cn: 动词和名词重音不同：attribute /əˈtrɪbjuːt/ 与 attribute /ˈætrɪbjuːt/。

normal.en: An attribute in grammar is a modifier: it gives a property to a noun, as in red car.
normal.cn: 语法中的 attribute 是修饰语：它把一个性质给名词，如 red car。
